en: Flow with your sweetest and most intoxicating stream, O Soma,
pressed for Indra to drink.
The slayer of demons, the observer of all people,
has sat upon his iron-fashioned seat with the wooden vessel at his dwelling place.
Be the best granter of wide space, the most bountiful, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra;
bring across the wealth of our patrons.
Flow toward the feast of the great gods with your juice;
flow toward strength and fame.
Toward you we move, for this very purpose day after day; O Indu, our hopes rest in you.
The daughter of the Sun purifies your flowing Soma with the eternal, continuous fleece.
The ten slender maidens, his sisters, seize him at the encounter on the decisive day.
The maidens urge him forth; they blow the leather bag like a bellows; [they prepare] the threefold, resistless honey.
The inviolable cows and the milch-kine mix this Soma, the infant, for Indra to drink.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], Indra slays all the Vṛtras; as a hero, he bestows riches.
Flow onward with speed through the filter, O Soma, winner of the gods;
O Indu, enter Indra as a bull.
Flow forth, O Indu, as a great draught, most resplendent bull;
as one who sustains all, sit upon your seat.
They have milked the beloved honey, the streams of the pressed juice of the wise one; the one of excellent power has clothed himself in the waters.
The great waters, the rivers, flow after you, the mighty one,
when you clothe yourself in the milk of cows.
The ocean has been purified in the waters, the support and sustainer of heaven; Soma, seeking us, is cleansed in the filter.
The tawny bull has bellowed; great and beautiful like Mitra, he shines together with the sun.
O Indu, your active songs are polished with power,
those by which you are adorned for exhilaration.
We implore you, the maker of wide space, for the sake of exhilarating joy;
great indeed are your praises.
O Indu, desiring Indra, flow for us with a stream of honey,
like Parjanya rich in rain.
O Indu, you are the winner of cattle, the winner of men, the winner of horses, and the winner of booty;
you are the primordial soul of the sacrifice.
This immortal god flies like a winged bird, to settle within the wooden vats.
This god, prepared by inspired hymns, flows across the obstacles;
he is Pavamāna, the invincible.
This god, Pavamāna, the tawny one, is purified for the sake of strength by those who praise him and love the cosmic order.
Like a hero going forth with his warriors, this Pavamāna seeks to win all desirable things.
This god, Pavamāna, speeds on his chariot;
he bestows gifts and makes his voice manifest.
Praised by the sages, this god plunges into the waters,
bestowing treasures upon the donor.
This Pavamāna, bellowing loudly, rushes through the sky across the regions with his stream.
This Pavamāna, the one who performs the excellent sacrifice, has spread across the sky, passing through the unassailable regions.
According to his ancient birth, this god, pressed for the gods,
the tawny one, flows through the filter.
This very one, of many vows, being born and generating strengthening foods, flows in a stream as the pressed juice.
O Soma, being purified, win and conquer great renown;
and so, make us more prosperous.
Winning back the light, winning back the sun, and all blessings, O Soma—
then make us more prosperous.
Winning skill and mental power, O Soma, strike away our adversaries;
then make us more prosperous.
O purifiers, purify the Soma for Indra to drink;
and then make us more prosperous.
Grant us our share in the sun through your wisdom and your protections;
then make us more prosperous.
By your wisdom and by your protections, may we long behold the sun;
and then, make us more prosperous.
Flow toward us, O Soma, well-armed one, with doubly great wealth;
and then make us more prosperous.
Flow toward us, O unshakable one, as a conqueror in battles;
and then make us more prosperous.
O Pavamāna, they have magnified you with sacrifices in this world;
therefore, make us more prosperous.
O Indu, bring us manifold wealth consisting of horses and full vitality;
then make us more prosperous.
Enkindled, the Lord on every side, Pavamāna shines forth,
the bull, bellowing loudly, bringing delight.
Tanūnapāt, the purifying one, flows onward sharpening his horns, shining brightly through the mid-air.
Worthy of invocation, the radiant Pavamāna shines forth as wealth,
with the streams of sweetness and with might.
Strewing the sacrificial grass toward the east with his might, the tawny Pavamāna,
as a god among the gods, goes forth.
The golden, divine doors have opened wide upward with their frames,
well-praised by Pavamāna.
Pavamāna yearns for the two great, vast, and well-fashioned ones, who are beautiful to behold like Night and Dawn.
I invoke both divine Hotṛ-priests who behold men;
Pavamāna and Indra, the bull.
May Bhāratī, Sarasvatī, and the great Ilā of the purifying one—
these three well-adorned goddesses— come to this sacrifice of ours.
I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the first-born guardian who goes before;
Indu is Indra, the bull, the golden-hued, the purifying Prajāpati.
O Pavamāna, anoint the Lord of the Forest with a stream of honey—
him who has a thousand branches, who is green, radiant, and golden.
O All-Gods, come to the consecration with the cry of *svāhā* of Pavamāna—
Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra, acting in harmony.
O Soma, flow with a pleasant stream as a bull, seeking the gods,
through the sheep’s wool, longing for us.
O Indu, flow toward that exhilarating intoxication, O Indra;
flow toward the prize-winning steeds.
Being pressed, flow toward that ancient exhilaration in the filter;
flow toward strength and fame.
The drops, the Soma-drops, have flowed along like waters down a slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.
Him whom the ten young women cleanse like a spirited steed, as he sports in the wood beyond the sheepskin filter.
Mix that bull-like juice with milk for exhilaration, for the feast of the gods, and for the sake of the pressed draught.
The god, pressed for the god Indra, flows forth, sustaining him,
so that his milk may swell.
The soul of the sacrifice, pressed for speed, flows as the effused juice;
he guards the ancient wisdom of the seers.
Thus, O most intoxicating one, being purified as one who desires Indra for the feast,
you have placed your songs even in the secret cave.
The beautiful drops have been poured forth according to the path and the law of Truth, knowing their course through this [sacrifice].
The foremost stream of honeyed mead plunges into the great waters;
he is the oblation among oblations, worthy of praise.
The foremost bull has bellowed toward the woods, releasing his voices;
he is the true sacrifice proceeding toward the dwellings.
When the sage, clothing himself in poetic wisdoms and manly powers, flows around,
the prize-winning steed seeks to win the light of heaven.
Pavamāna sits over the rival clans like a king when the wise ones set him in motion.
The beloved tawny one sits within the woody filters upon the sheep’s wool; as a singer, he is implored with a hymn.
Accompanied by exhilaration, he goes to Vāyu, Indra, and the Aśvins,
he who delights in his laws.
The waves of the sweet [Soma] flow toward Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga,
made known by its powers.
O Heaven and Earth, win for us wealth, the sweetness of nourishment, and glory, so that we may acquire riches and treasures.
These Soma juices have flowed forth toward the beloved desire of Indra,
increasing his heroic power.
Being purified, seated in the vessels, and going toward Vāyu and the Aśvins—
may they bestow upon us great heroic strength.
O Soma, being purified, incite the heart of Indra for the sake of bounty,
so that you may sit upon the seat of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
The ten fingers cleanse you; the seven prayers impel you; the sages have rejoiced after you.
Thee, being released through the sheep’s fleece for the exhilaration of the gods,
we clothe with the milk of cows.
Being purified in the jars, the ruddy, tawny one has clothed himself in garments made of milk.
Flow for us from the bountiful one; strike away all enemies.
O Indu, enter into your friend.
Flow down the rain from heaven; bestow splendor upon the earth;
O Soma, grant us strength in battles.
May we partake of you, who beholds men, who are drunk by Indra, and who finds the light of heaven— may we obtain offspring and nourishment.
The sage of heaven, having been placed between the two daughters, goes forth being pressed, bestowing dear vital strengths; he moves with the wisdom of a seer.
Flow on and on for the dwelling that is most praiseworthy, beloved by the guileless folk;
flow with most delightful nourishment.
He, the pure son, as soon as he was born, caused his two parents to shine; great, he illumined the two great ones who increase the cosmic order.
Urged on by the seven prayers, he has quickened the guileless rivers,
which have magnified the single eye.
They have established him, the unconquered and mighty youth,
the drop (indu), within your service, O Indra.
The immortal bearer, swiftly carrying [the oblation], beholds the seven;
Krivi has satisfied the goddesses.
O Soma, protect us in our strivings; O Purifier, strike down those darknesses that must be fought.
Now, for our newest and most recent hymn, prepare the paths; as of old, cause the lights to shine.
O Pavamāna, grant us great renown, cattle, horses, and heroic sons;
win for us wisdom and win the light of heaven.
Resounding like chariots, like horses seeking glory,
the Soma drops have flowed forth for the sake of wealth.
Urged onward like chariots, they have sped forth from the hands,
like the prizes of those who perform sacred rites.
Like kings with praises, the Soma drops are anointed with milk,
like a sacrifice by the seven ordainers.
Being pressed for exhilaration with a mighty song, O drops, the juices flow in a stream once they have been poured out.
Drinking from Vivasvat, they have generated the fortune of the Dawn;
like heroes, they spread across the fine [sieve].
The ancient singers open the doors of hymns for the manly one,
as living men [open the gates] for the impetuous might of the bull.
The seven co-born priests sit together in harmony; they fill out the station of the One.
I have joined my navel with your navel, as the eye is united with the sun;
the offspring of the Seer yields its milk.
The Sun beholds with his eye the dear place of heaven, hidden in the secret cave by the Adhvaryu priests.
Sing forth, O men, to this Indu as he purifies himself;
he seeks to reach the gods.
The Atharvans have fortified your milk with honey,
O god who yearns for the gods, for the sake of the god.
As such, flow pure for us, bringing well-being to our cattle, well-being to our people, and well-being to our horses; O King, bring well-being to the plants.
Now sing a song to Soma, the tawny one, who is self-strong, ruddy, and touches the heavens.
Purify the pressed Soma with stones moved by the hands;
pour the honey into the honey.
Approach with reverence; mix [the soma] with curds;
place the *indu* within Indra.
O Soma, slayer of enemies, most active among men, flow clear for the welfare of our cattle,
fulfilling the desires of the gods.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra to drink, for his exhilaration— you who are mindful,
the lord of the mind.
O Pavamāna Soma, bestow upon us wealth consisting of heroic strength;
O Indu, together with Indra as our ally.
The Soma drops have been poured forth, the pressed juices, at the seat of Ṛta,
most sweet for Indra.
The sages have sung forth to Indra for the drinking of the Soma, as mother cows low toward their calf.
Dropping exhilaration, the wise Soma dwells in his seat upon the wave of the river,
resting upon the two white cows.
Far-sighted at the navel of heaven, Soma, the wise seer of excellent insight, is magnified within the fleece of the sheep.
That Soma which has been placed within the jars, inside the filter— Indu has embraced it from all sides.
The drop sends forth its voice upon the surface of the ocean,
enlivening the honey-dripping vessel.
The Lord of the Forest, whose praise is eternal, the yielder of plenty within our prayers,
impels the generations of men.
Urged on, Soma, the seer, flows toward the dear places of heaven with the stream of the inspired singer.
O Pavamāna, bestow upon us wealth of a thousandfold splendor, O Indu, that which is self-sustaining.
Soma, being purified, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool,
to the appointed place of Vāyu and Indra.
O seekers of aid, sing forth to Pavamāna, the inspired sage,
who has been pressed for the banquet of the gods.
The Soma juices, possessing thousandfold power, are purified for the winning of booty,
being praised for the banquet of the gods.
And flow for us, O Indu, for the winning of booty, bringing great nourishment, radiant splendor, and heroic strength.
May those divine drops, being pressed, flow for us with thousandfold wealth and excellent heroic power.
Like horses urged on by their drivers, the swift ones have been let loose through the sheep’s wool filter for the winning of the prize.
The lowing drops flow like milch-cows toward their calf; they have run forth from the hands.
O Pavamāna, being exhilarating and pleasing to Indra, bellowing loudly,
strike away all our enemies.
Driving away the stingy ones, O purifying Soma-drops who behold the light of heaven,
sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
The sage has flowed all around, resting upon the wave of the river,
bearing the much-desired song of praise.
When the five kindred hosts, active in their work, with song adorn the Sustainer; RV_9.014.02c–d. When the five kindred hosts, active in their work, with song adorn the Sustainer.
Then all the gods have become exhilarated by the juice of this impetuous one,
when he clothes himself in the products of the cow.
Rushing forth, he runs away, casting off his arrows and his body; there he is struck down by his companion.
He who, like a bright youth, has been groomed by the granddaughters of Vivasvat,
making the cows his own garment.
Passing beyond the two oblique crossings, he goes forth seeking cattle through the fine [strainer];
he utters the sound which he has found.
The swift fingers have gathered together, purifying the Lord of Strength;
seize the backs of the prize-winning steed.
O Soma, stroking all divine and earthly treasures, come toward us, seeking us.
This hero goes with subtle wisdom and with swift chariots,
proceeding to the appointed place of Indra.
He meditates with many thoughts upon the great assembly of the gods,
where the immortals dwell.
This [Soma], once set in motion, is led forth along the path of the radiant one,
when the impetuous ones urge him on.
This bull of the herd, shaking his horns, whets them;
bestowing manly powers by his might.
This vigorous one moves along with his golden ornaments, with his bright rays,
becoming the lord of the rivers.
This one, having passed through the firm joints of the rugged [mountains],
goes down into the resting places.
Men cleanse him who is worthy of cleansing within the wooden vats;
he who brings forth great nourishments.
Him, indeed, the ten fingers and the seven prayers cleanse—
him who is well-armed and most intoxicating.
O pressers, pour forth your juice for your exhilaration, for the impetuous one; like a released steed, Etaśa hastens on.
Through the power of skill, we have followed the charioteer of dexterity, who clothes himself in the waters with his juice—
the winner of cattle among the fine [strainers].
Release the unassailable Soma, difficult to cross over, into the waters upon the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink.
With the mind of one being purified, Soma flows through the filter; by his power of will, he has taken his seat in the common dwelling-place.
The Soma drops, O Indra, have been poured forth for you with prostrations,
like performers striving for a great prize.
Being purified in the eternal form, flowing toward all splendors,
he stands among the cattle like a hero.
Like the swelling ridge of heaven, the stream of the pressed juice of the Ordainer flows freely through the filter.
O Soma, being purified through the lineage among living beings, you, the inspired one,
flow through the sheep’s wool filter.
Like rivers flowing down a slope, the impetuous Soma drops, swiftly destroying the Vṛtras, have been let loose.
Like rains upon the earth, the pressed Soma drops have flowed toward Indra.
Surging over the waves, exhilarating and intoxicating, the Soma flows through the filter,
warding off the demons while seeking the gods.
He rushes into the jars; he is poured out across the filter;
he grows strong at the sacrifices through the hymns of praise.
O Soma, ascending above the three luminous realms, you shine like heaven; sending forth your rays, you impel the sun.
The inspired poets, the singers, have sung aloud at the head of the sacrifice,
bestowing what is dear upon your sight.
Thee, the prize-winning one, the sages and inspired poets, seeking aid, cleanse with their prayers for the sake of the gods.
Flow along the stream of honey; as something potent, take your seat upon the common dwelling-place, beautiful for the sake of the Truth and for drinking.
Being pressed, Soma, dwelling on the mountains, has flowed through the filter; in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
You are the inspired singer, you are the seer; the honey is born from the soma-juice. In your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
All the gods, acting in harmony with you, have attained the drinking of you; in your exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
He who holds in his hands all desirable treasures— you are the bestower of everything in the exhilarations of Soma.
He who milks these two great worlds, like two mother-cows;
in thy exhilarations, thou art the bestower of all.
He who flows instantly around both worlds with his strengths— you are the bestower of all things in the exhilarations of the soma.
He, the impetuous one, has bellowed within the jars while being purified;
in the exhilarations, you are the bestower of all things.
O Soma, as you are being purified, bring us that wonderful, hymn-worthy wealth which is celestial and terrestrial.
For you two are the lords of heaven, O Indra and Soma, the masters of cattle;
as sovereign rulers, cause our prayers to swell with abundance.
The bull, being purified among the living, thundering upon the sacred grass— being tawny, he has settled in his place.
The prayers have lowed over the seed of the bull;
the mothers [low] for their son, the calf.
As he purifies himself, does he not indeed bestow the germ upon those longing for a bull—
those who yield the bright milk?
Bestow fear upon the enemies who stand aloof;
O Pavamāna, find wealth for us.
O Soma, strike down the virility of the enemy, strike down his strength, and strike down his vital power,
whether he be far away or near at hand.
The sage flows forth through the sheep’s woolly fleece for the feast of the gods,
overcoming all rivalrous foes.
For he, indeed, as Pavamāna, bestows upon his singers thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle.
You touch all things with your mind; you flow clear through our hymns. O Soma, as such, find for us glorious renown.
Flow forth toward great glory and stable wealth for the patrons;
bring nourishment to those who praise you.
O wondrous bearer of the oblation, being purified, O Soma, you have entered the songs like a king who observes his sacred vows.
That Soma, the invoker difficult to overcome in the waters, being cleansed by the two hands, sits within the vessels.
Sportive like a generous sacrificer, O Soma, you go to the filter,
bestowing great heroic strength upon the singer.
These Soma drops run toward Indra, exhilarating and joyous, finding the light of heaven.
Driving away assailants for the one who presses the soma, finding wide space, they themselves bestow vigor upon the singer.
Playing freely, the drops have flowed together toward their single common dwelling;
they have poured forth in the wave of the river.
These purifying drops have attained all desirable things, like well-harnessed horses yoked to a chariot.
O drops, bestow upon this man a tawny,
longing [desire] to point out him who is ungenerous toward us.
Like Ṛbhu, bestow a new chariot for our purpose;
O bright ones, flow forth with your flood.
These very ones have lowed; the prize-winners have reached the goal;
they have poured forth the thought of the existent one.
These swift Soma drops have sped forth like chariots, like prize-winning steeds, released in their courses.
Like winds, they are wide-reaching; like the rains of Parjanya, they are impetuous; like the flickering flames of fire, they move with ease.
These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curds,
have pervaded the prayers through inspired thought.
These immortal ones, purified and having flowed forth, have not grown weary;
desiring to sacrifice, they traverse the paths through the mid-air.
These [Soma drops], moving as priests, have pervaded the heights of heaven and earth,
and even this highest realm.
They have followed along the downward slopes the highest thread being stretched out;
and this is most worthy of praise.
O Soma, you held for us the wealth of cattle from the Paṇis;
you made the stretched-out thread resound.
The swift Soma drops have been poured forth in a stream of honeyed exhilaration,
toward all poetic insights.
The ancient Āyus have followed after the newest footprint;
they brought forth the Sun for the sake of splendor.
O Pavamāna, bring us the wealth of the non-sacrificing enemy;
provide us with nourishments that bring forth progeny.
The Soma-drops, the active ones, flow toward the intoxicating exhilaration,
toward the honey-dripping vat.
Soma flows, the sustainer, bestowing vital power and essence;
he is the possessor of noble heroes and the protector against curses.
O Soma, you flow for Indra, for the gods, as one who shares the feast;
O Indu, you desire to win us strength.
Having drunk of his exhilarating draughts, Indra, irresistible against the Vṛtras,
has slain them and shall slay them yet again.
The Soma drops have flowed forth, the purifying juices;
being mixed with milk, they are cleansed in the waters.
The cows have run forth toward him like waters flowing down a slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.
O Pavamāna Soma, you flow forth for Indra to drink;
guided by the men, you are led out.
O Soma, flow as the exhilarator of men, for the sake of one who overcomes the peoples— thou who art a winner of prizes and worthy of universal acclaim.
O Indu, when pressed by the stones, you run through the filter,
well-suited for the abode of Indra.
Flow on, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, to be celebrated with hymns—
pure, purifying, and wonderful.
Pure and purifying, the pressed Soma of the sweet mead is called the one who favors the gods and slays the wicked.
Flow on, O tawny one, accomplishing skillful power for the gods to drink;
flow as a gladdening draught for the Maruts and for Vāyu.
O Pavamāna, impelled by the prayer, crying out toward your place of origin,
enter Vāyu according to the cosmic law.
The bull, the sage, the beloved, shines together with the gods upon his seat;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest invoker of the gods.
Entering all forms, the beloved one goes forth while being purified,
to where the immortals sit.
The ruddy Soma, engendering songs, flows on for the sake of long life,
going toward Indra with the wisdom of a seer.
Flow, O most exhilarating sage, through the filter with your stream, to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
The sages have groomed that vigorous steed upon the lap of Aditi with their subtle meditation.
The cows have lowed toward him, the inexhaustible one with a thousand streams—
the drop (*indu*), the sustainer from heaven.
They have brought that creator, Pavamāna, by means of wisdom to the sky—
the sustainer, the one who provides abundant nourishment.
They have sent him forth with prayer from the two arms, him who dwells together with Vivasvat,
the infallible lord of speech.
The sisters urge him, the golden-hued, upon the mountain ridge with the pressing-stones—
the beloved one who gazes far and wide.
The wise priests urge you on, O Pavamāna, you who increase with song—
O Indu, the exhilarating draught for Indra.
This seer, highly praised, flows over the filter; being purified, he strikes away the adversaries.
This winner of light, the accomplisher of skill, is poured out for Indra and Vāyu within the filter.
This Soma, the head of heaven, the bull, pressed by men, is led forth through the wooden vessels; he is the knower of all things.
This Pavamāna, seeking cattle and seeking gold, has bellowed;
Indu is the ever-conquering, the invincible.
This Pavamāna, the exhilarating intoxicant, shines with the sun in heaven as he flows through the filter.
This vigorous, tawny bull has flowed through the mid-air; being purified, the drop goes toward Indra.
This prize-winning steed, sent forth by men, the all-knowing lord of the mind,
rushes through the sheep’s wool filter.
This Soma, pressed for the gods, has flowed through the filter,
entering all the sacred abodes.
This immortal god shines forth upon his station;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the one most beloved by the gods.
This bull, bellowing loudly, guided by the ten sisters,
rushes toward the wooden vats.
This Pavamāna, the all-seeing and all-knowing, has caused the sun to shine and has illuminated all the realms.
This powerful, invincible Soma flows while being purified; he is the friend of the gods and the slayer of the wicked.
His streams have flowed forth by the might of the pressed bull,
as he stands ready to serve the gods.
The wise singers, chanting with their song, groom the steed—
the light that has been born, worthy of praise.
O Soma, Lord of Abundance, these things are easy for you to overcome as you purify yourself; increase the ocean that is worthy of praise.
Winning all treasures, flow on with your stream, O Soma;
drive away our enemies together.
Protect us well from the malicious man, from the shout of anyone whatsoever, so that we may be released from reproach.
O Soma, flow with your stream, purifying the earthly and celestial wealth;
bring us brilliant vigor.
The streams of this impetuous one have flowed freely through the filter; purifying himself, he sends forth his voice.
The drop, urged by the pressers and being cleansed while bellowing,
sends forth the voice of Indra.
Flow for us, O Soma, with your stream— our strength that conquers men, rich in heroes, and much-desired.
Soma, being purified, has flowed forth with his stream,
to settle within the wooden vats.
In the waters they urge you on with the stones— the honey-sweet, golden-hued one—
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most honey-sweet Soma; press it as a lovely, exhilarating draught for the host.
The Soma drops, well-intentioned and purifying, have moved forward;
they create wealth that brings consciousness.
O Indu, from heaven and from earth, be the increaser of our splendor;
become the lord of spoils.
For you the winds blow favorably; for you the rivers flow;
O Soma, they increase your greatness.
Swell up; let virile strength come to you from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of the prize.
For you, O tawny one, the cows have milked out imperishable ghee and milk upon the highest summit.
O Indu, Lord of the world, we desire your friendship— you who are well-armed.
The Soma drops, distilling exhilaration, have flowed forth for the glory of our patrons, pressed out at the assembly.
Then the maidens of Trita urge the tawny one with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Then, like a swan to its flock, he has caused the prayer of every man to resound;
like a steed, he is anointed with milk.
O Soma, looking down upon both worlds, you flow like a darting deer,
settling into the womb of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
The cows have lowed toward him, as a woman toward her beloved; he has gone to the race as if to a prize already set.
Bestow upon us resplendent glory, for the sake of the patrons and for me; grant us gain, wisdom, and renown.
The wise Soma drops go forth like waves of water,
like buffaloes toward the forests.
The tawny, bright drops have flowed toward the wooden vats with the stream of Truth,
pouring forth strength consisting of cattle.
The pressed Soma juices flow for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, the Maruts, and Viṣṇu.
Three voices rise up; the cows low as milch-kine;
the tawny one goes along bellowing.
The youthful mothers of the Eternal Order, the divine ones, have sung aloud;
they groom him, the Child of Heaven.
O Soma, flow for us from every side with riches that are like the four oceans, bringing thousandsfold wealth.
Being pressed, Indu flows forth in a stream, speeding along; with his might, he breaks through even the firmest things.
Pressed for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts,
Soma flows for Viṣṇu.
They press the bull-like Soma with stones, guided by bulls; they milk the milk with skillful power.
May he be worthy of being cleansed by Trita; may he be intoxicating for Indra.
The tawny one is anointed with his forms.
The sons of Pṛśni milk him, the summit of Truth,
the lovely and most beloved oblation.
These unerring songs flow together toward him;
the lowing one has made the cows low.
Flow for us with your stream, O Pavamāna, bestowing vast wealth,
by which you may find light for us.
O Indu, swayer of the ocean, flow on, O all-shaker; as the upholder of wealth, protect us with your might.
With you as our hero, O Hero, may we overcome those who attack us; let there flow for us what is desirable.
The drop speeds forth toward strength, the seer desiring to win, seeking to gain the prize; he knows the sacred laws and his weapons.
With our songs we clothe him, the swayer of speech, as he purifies himself—
the Soma, the lord of the people.
He under whose law all people abide, the Lord of Dharma, as he is being purified, O possessor of abundant wealth.
Like a chariot-horse, the pressed juice has been released into the filter from the two bowls; like a prize-winning steed, it has stepped forth to the goal.
O Soma, as the wakeful bearer, flow across [the filter] for the gods,
toward the honey-dripping vat.
O ancient Pavamāna, cause these lights of ours to shine forth; impel us toward wisdom and skill.
Being beautified by those who love the *ṛta*, and being cleansed by the two hands,
he flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
May that Soma flow for the donor, bestowing all treasures— those of heaven, those of the earth, and those of the intermediate space.
O Soma, Lord of Might, seeking horses and seeking cattle, you ascend to the back of heaven; seeking heroes, you rise up.
Pressed for the sake of drinking, that bull-like Soma flows through the filter,
warding off the demons and seeking the gods.
The far-seeing, tawny one, the sustainer, flows through the filter,
bellowing toward his place of origin.
That vigorous one, Pavamāna, rushes through the luminous realms of heaven,
the slayer of demons, across the fleece of the sheep.
Pavamāna, upon the ridge of Trita, caused the sun to shine together with his kinsmen.
That Soma, the slayer of Vṛtra, the bull, the pressed one, the finder of wide space, the invincible, has flowed forth like booty.
That god, impelled by the seer, rushes toward the wooden vats—
the drop for Indra, with great bounty.
This very bull, this chariot, flows through the sheep’s woolly filter,
going toward thousandfold booty.
The maidens of Trita urge this tawny one with the pressing-stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Him, the one, the ten active fingers cleanse;
with those [fingers] by which he is adorned for exhilaration.
Like a falcon settling among the human clans, he sits down; like a lover going to his mistress, he hastens toward them.
This exhilarating juice, the child of heaven, looks down from on high—
this Soma-drop that has entered the filter.
This golden one, pressed for drinking, flows as a steadfast supporter; crying out, he hastens toward his beloved dwelling-place.
Flow swiftly, O you of lofty thought, with your beloved form,
to where they cry out, "The gods!"
Preparing what was unprepared, bringing forth nourishment for the people,
flow down from heaven as rain.
The pressed juice goes into the filter, assuming brilliance by its might,
looking out and shining forth.
This is he who, with rapid course, from heaven has flowed through the filter;
he has poured forth upon the wave of the river.
Inviting [the gods] from afar and from nearby,
the pressed honey is poured for Indra.
Turning together, they have sung; they urge the tawny one with the stones;
sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
Being purified, the far-seeing one has stepped upon all adversaries;
they adorn the inspired singer with their prayers.
The ruddy one has mounted his place; the pressed bull goes to Indra;
he settles in his firm seat.
Now, O Indu, flow forth for us from every side, O Soma, bringing great wealth in thousands.
O Soma Pavamāna, O Indu, bring hither all splendors;
find for us nourishments in thousands.
As you are being purified, bring us wealth and heroic strength for our singer; increase the songs of the one who praises you.
O Indu, being purified, O Soma, bring us doubly-mighty wealth;
O virile Indu, bring us that which is worthy of praise.
Those who have advanced like restless bulls, impetuous and tireless,
driving away the black skin.
We meditate upon a path to well-being that crosses over the bridge of the godless,
as we overcome the lawless Dasyu.
The roar of the mighty Pavamāna is heard like the sound of rain;
lightnings flash across the sky.
Flow forth, O Indu, as pressed juice, bringing great nourishment, rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses, and rich in booty.
Flow on, O you who observe all people; fill the two great worlds, heaven and earth, as the Dawn and the Sun fill them with their rays.
O Soma, flow around us on every side with a stream that grants protection,
as rivers flow toward the heights.
Generating the luminous realms of heaven and generating the sun within the waters,
the tawny one, clothed in milk and water, flows on.
According to the ancient hymn, this god, pressed out for the sake of the gods,
flows forth in a stream.
For the one who has grown strong and overcomes, for the winning of the prize, the Soma juices with their thousandfold power flow clear.
Yielding his ancient milk, he is poured out across the filter;
crying out, he has brought the gods into being.
Soma, being purified, flows toward all desirable things and toward the gods who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
O Soma, being pressed, flow for us with wealth in cattle, in heroes, in horses, and in booty;
flow forth abundant nourishments.
He who, like a steed, is cleansed by the milk-cows for exhilaration, he who is desirable—
him we clothe with our songs.
All our songs, seeking his aid, adorn him as of old—
for Indra, to drink the drop.
Being purified, the beloved Soma goes forth, adorned with songs, [the work] of the inspired Medhyātithi.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth accompanied by great splendor;
O Indu, [find] that which possesses a thousandfold luster.
Like a steed seeking booty, Indu bellows loudly in the filter as he flows across,
longing for the gods.
Flow on for the winning of strength, for the increase of the sage who praises you; O Soma, bestow upon us heroic power.
O Indu, bearing [the Soma] like a wave for our great expansion, flow forth toward the gods, you who are unwearied.
Pleased by our hymns and impelled by our prayer, Soma, the sage, is driven forth in the distance by the stream of the inspired singer.
This Soma, watchful among the gods, goes pressed into the filter; the far-seeing one flows onward.
Flow for us, seeking booty, making our sacrifice beautiful;
the one who provides the sacrificial grass invites you hither.
May Soma, the hero among sages, ever-increasing, direct us toward Bhaga, Vāyu, and the gods.
May he, who finds the way and bestows wisdom, win for us today great renown and strength for the sake of obtaining wealth.
Flow on for exhilaration, O you who behold men, for the banquet of the gods;
flow, O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Flow for us toward the mission of a messenger; you bestow gifts upon Indra, bringing the gods as a boon to our friends.
And we anoint you, the ruddy one, with milk for exhilaration;
open wide for us the doors to wealth.
The prize-winner has passed through the filter like a horse to its harness on the path;
Indu rules among the gods.
Together the friends have shouted for him as he sports in the wood beyond the sheepskin;
they have sung to Indu with a boat.
Flow with that stream by which, when drunk, O Indu, you bestow great heroic power upon the singer.
The swift ones have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like successful warriors,
flowing forth, increasing upon the mountains.
Adorned like a maiden seeking her father's house,
the Soma drops have been poured forth toward Vāyu.
These Soma drops, full of nourishment, pressed into the vessels,
strengthen Indra with their ritual acts.
O dexterous ones, run hither; seize the bright juices with the *manthin* vessel;
mix the exhilarating draught with milk.
Flow on, O winner of wealth, bestowing great riches;
O Soma, find the path for us.
The ten fingers cleanse this Pavamāna who is worthy of being cleansed—
the exhilarating intoxicant for Indra.
By this skillful act, Soma has grown even greater; exhilarated, he exerts himself like a bull.
His deeds that were done and those yet to be done are manifest as the subduing of the Dasyus;
and the bold one exacts the debts.
Then, O Soma, the Indra-powering juice becomes a thousand-winning thunderbolt when his hymn of praise is born.
The poet himself, as the distributor, seeks a treasure for the sage when he thoroughly polishes his prayers.
You are the one who desires to win riches, like the prize-winning steeds in races, among those who are victorious in battles.
We approach you, who bear manly powers in the gathering places of the great heaven,
the lovely one, with our skillful work.
The exhilarating drink, which has gathered boldness, is worthy of praise, possesses most mighty ordinances,
and desires to shatter a hundred fortresses.
From there, O wise one, the unwavering, well-winged bird has brought you, the king of wealth, from heaven.
For every one to behold the light, the hero has brought forth the common guardian of Truth, who traverses the mid-air.
Then, being urged forth, he attained greater Indra-power and majesty—
he who bestows aid and observes all people.
Flow for us, bringing rain from the heavens, a wave of waters;
bring health-bestowing, abundant nourishments.
Flow with that stream by which the cows belonging to the people have come here to our house.
Flow with a stream of clarified butter, you who are most beloved by the gods at the sacrifices;
pour down rain upon us.
Flow for us with your stream through the sheep’s-wool filter for the sake of nourishment;
may the gods indeed hear us!
Pavamāna has flowed forth, striking down the demons, illuminating splendors as he did of old.
Your vital energies surge forth like the roar of a river's wave;
sharpen the point of your arrow.
At your impulsion, three voices eager for the sacrifice rise up,
when you go upon the back of the sheep’s wool.
They urge the beloved tawny one through the sheep’s wool with stones— the purifying one who drips with sweetness.
Flow, O most exhilarating sage, through the filter in a stream, to sit upon the seat of the hymn.
Flow on, O most intoxicating one, anointed with milk and with ointments,
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
O Adhvaryu, pour the Soma pressed with stones into the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink.
Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most excellent nectar of heaven, the Soma most rich in sweetness.
O Indu, those gods and the Maruts partake of this sweet juice of yours, of you as you flow clear.
For you, O Soma, being pressed for the wild exhilaration, do thou,
O bull, strengthen the praiser for his protection.
Flow toward the filter with your stream, O far-seeing one, pressed for the sake of booty and renown.
Winning wealth from heaven, may he who dwells in light bring us strength with his juice;
being pressed, flow into the filter.
By your ancient paths, the beloved one flows through the sheep’s wool filter,
moving in a continuous stream with a thousandfold current.
O Indu, swing him like a ladle; O giver, swing thy gift;
O wielder of weapons, swing [thy] blows with thy weapons.
O Indu, invoked by many, bring down the vigor of these people who direct their intent against us.
O Indu, flow for us with a hundred aids, or even a thousand of your pure streams; bestowing wealth, purify yourself.
Your vital powers have risen up, O wielder of the stone, shattering the demons;
drive away those who are our rivals.
With this [song], you who strike down [the foe] by your might when chariots clash and the prize is staked,
you are praised with a fearless heart.
The ordinances of this Pavamāna cannot be assailed by one of evil intent; shatter him who attacks you.
They drive him, the exhilarating, tawny, prize-winning steed, into the rivers— the Indu, the intoxicant for Indra.
Following his ancient splendor, the bold ones have milked the bright milk from the seer who wins a thousandfold.
This one is visible like the sun; he rushes toward the lakes and the seven downward-flowing rivers unto heaven.
Purifying himself, this Soma stands above all worlds like the divine Sun.
Flow around us for the feast of the gods, O Indu, bringing strengths rich in cattle, as you are purified, longing for Indra.
O Soma, flow around us with your juice, grain by grain, nourishment by nourishment, and all auspicious blessings.
O Indu, just as there is praise for you, and just as there is the production of your juice,
so may you sit upon the beloved sacrificial grass.
And, O Soma, finding cattle and finding horses, flow for us with your juice through these most rapid days.
He who conquers and is never conquered, who attacks and slays the enemy— O winner of thousands, flow on as such.
O Soma, the swift one, flowing through the filter, purifies the lofty *ṛta*,
striking down the demons and seeking the gods.
When Soma flows toward the prize in a hundred active streams,
he enters into friendship with Indra.
The ten young women have sung out to you like a maiden to her lover; O Soma, you are cleansed for the sake of winning the prize.
O Indu, flow forth as something sweet for Indra and Viṣṇu;
protect the men, the singers, from distress.
Your unceasing streams go forth like rains from heaven,
toward thousandfold booty.
Beholding all beloved poetic insights, he flows onward;
the tawny one, brandishing his weapons.
Being cleansed by the Āyus, like a king who observes his vows, he, the wild beast,
settles among the woods like a hawk.
As you are being purified, O Indu, bring to us all treasures from heaven and from the earth.
Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows; the stream of the pressed juice flows;
crossing over, the exhilarating one flows.
The Dawn knows of the treasures; the Goddess knows the aid for the mortal. Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows swiftly.
From the two Dhvasras, the lords of men, we receive thousands;
crossing over, that exhilarating one flows swiftly.
He for whom we bestow thirty thousand in succession—
he, the exhilarating one, speeds across.
Flow on, O Soma, winner of cattle, winner of horses, winner of all, winner of delight;
bring us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Flow pure for the waters, O invincible one; flow pure for the plants;
flow pure for the sacred vessels.
O Soma, as you flow clear, cross over all difficulties;
as a seer, sit down upon the sacred grass.
O Pavamāna, finder of light, being born you became great;
O Indu, you are indeed superior to all.
Sing forth with the *gāyatra* chant to Pavamāna,
the all-beholding, to Indu, the thousand-eyed.
Thee, who hast a thousand eyes and who bringest a thousandfold wealth— thus have they purified thee through the filter.
Pavamāna has flowed across the woollen filters; he rushes toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra.
O Soma, most active one, flow clearly for the prosperity of Indra;
bring us seed accompanied by progeny.
Flow forth for this enjoyment, O Indu, which in thy exhilarations has struck down ninety-nine [enemies].
Immediately before this, for the sake of Divodāsa who thus meditated, you struck down Śambara,
as well as that Turvaśa and Yadu.
O Indu, finder of horses, flow for us with horses, with cattle, and with gold;
pour forth thousandfold nourishments.
We choose for ourselves the friendship of you, Pavamāna, as you flow toward the filter.
O Soma, those waves of yours which flow toward us with their stream through the filter—
through them, O Soma, show us mercy.
O Soma, being purified, bring to us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons; for you, O Lord, are the master over all.
Him, whose mother is the river, the ten fingers cleanse;
he has been beheld together with the Ādityas.
The pressed juice goes together with Indra and Vāyu into the filter;
it goes together with the rays of the sun.
Flow for us as honey-sweet for Bhaga, Vāyu, and Pūṣan; flow as one dear to Mitra and Varuṇa.
High is the birth of your juice; seated in heaven, it has been taken to earth—your fierce protection and great renown.
Through these [Somas], we, desiring to win, acquire all the glories of the noble one and of human beings.
Flow forth, finding wide space, for that Indra who is worthy of sacrifice, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts.
The gods have come near to the pressed drop, the son of the waters, who has been adorned with milk and is the breaker of obstacles.
May our songs increase him, as mother cows nourish their calf—
he who wins the heart of Indra.
Flow for us, O Soma, as a blessing for our cattle; milk out for us swelling nourishment; increase the ocean that is worthy of praise.
Pavamāna has generated for us the great light of Vaiśvānara, like a wondrous thunder from heaven.
O King, the exhilarating juice of you, Pavamāna, which brings no misfortune,
flows through the sheep’s wool filter.
O Pavamāna, your juice, your skillful and radiant power, shines forth;
it is all-light, the sun, for all to see.
With that exhilarating juice of yours which is most excellent, flow clear,
O god-favoring one, as a slayer of those who speak evil.
Slayer of Vṛtra and of the unfriendly, winner of booty day by day,
you are the winner of cattle and the winner of horses.
Become mingled with the ruddy ones, like cows easy to tend;
sit down like a hawk upon its nest.
Flow on, you who aided Indra to slay Vṛtra,
who had obstructed the great waters.
O bountiful Soma, may we, possessing brave sons, win riches;
as you are being purified, increase our songs of praise.
Aided by you and through your protection, may we be victors over those who attack; O Soma, be watchful over our sacred observances.
Striking down the adversaries, Soma flows clear,
driving away the stingy ones as he goes to the appointed place of Indra.
O Pavamāna, bring us great wealth; strike down our enemies.
O Indu, grant us glory accompanied by heroic sons.
Not even a hundred deceivers could diminish you as you desire to bestow bounty,
when, being purified, you act like a sacrificial steed.
Flow clear, O Indu, as the pressed bull; make us glorious among the people;
strike away all our enemies.
In this friendship of yours, O Indu, and in your supreme splendor, may we overcome those who attack us.
Those terrible weapons of yours that are sharp for striking down—
protect us from every reproach.
These swift drops of Soma have been poured through the filter toward all auspicious blessings.
Warding off many misfortunes, O swift ones, you provide easy passage for our offspring; by your continuous flow, you create prosperity for the steed.
Creating wide space for the cattle, they flow toward our fair praise; may they grant us constant nourishment.
The stalk has been pressed for intoxication in the waters—the skillful one dwelling on the mountains; like a hawk, he has settled in his place.
The bright Soma, the food of the gods, shaken in the waters and pressed by men—
cows sweeten it with their milk.
Then, like drivers [beautifying] a horse, they have adorned him for immortality—
the essence of honey, at the shared feast.
O Indu, those streams of yours that flow dripping with sweetness for our aid— with those you have settled upon the filter.
He flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece for Indra to drink,
settling in his place within the wooden vessels.
O Indu, flow around for the Aṅgirases as the sweetest one;
finding wide space, flow with ghee and milk.
This Pavamāna, the far-seeing one, being established, takes notice; being urged forward, he manifests his great kinship.
This bull, whose law is manly, Pavamāna, the slayer of the ill-spoken,
shall bestow riches upon the donor.
Flow forth, purifying yourself, bringing thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle and horses,
most radiant and much-desired.
This very one is poured out all around, being cleansed by the *āyu* priests— he who strides widely, possessing the wisdom of a seer.
With a thousand aids and a hundredfold wealth, the measurer of the mid-air, the sage,
the exhilarating juice flows for Indra.
Born here through song, the drop, praised, is placed for Indra like a hero in his dwelling-place.
Being pressed by the men, Pavamāna Soma has flowed forth like prize-winning strength, to sit within the vessels with his power.
Him they yoke upon the triple-backed, triple-seated chariot to go forth,
by means of the seven seers' inspired thoughts.
O pressers, urge on that tawny steed, the winner of wealth, swift to go for the prize.
Entering the jar, the pressed juice flows toward all splendors; like a hero among cattle, he stands firm.
O Indu, the Āyus milk out the milk for your exhilaration;
the gods [milk] the honey for the gods.
Pour forth for us into the filter the Soma most rich in sweetness, the one most renowned among the gods, for the sake of the gods.
These Soma juices have been poured forth, being praised for great renown,
with the stream of the most intoxicating one.
Being purified, you flow toward the cattle and manly powers for our enjoyment; winning the prize, flow around us.
And flow for us with all food-offerings accompanied by cattle,
being praised by Jamadagni.
Flow on as the leader of speech, O Soma, with your wondrous aids,
toward all poetic inspirations.
O you who stir the waters of the ocean, the foremost of speech, flow on,
O you who cause all things to tremble!
O Sage, these worlds stand ready for your greatness, O Soma;
for you the rivers flow.
Like showers from heaven, your unceasing streams flow forth toward the bright surface-covering.
Purify the Soma-drop for Indra, the fierce one, the accomplisher of strength,
the sovereign lord who bestows abundant wealth.
Pavamāna, the sage of Truth, Soma has sat upon the filter,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer.
Flow on, O Soma, bringing thousandfold wealth and heroic strength; bestow upon us glorious renown.
O most intoxicating one, you swell with nourishment and vigor for Indra; you settle down within the vessels.
The pressed Soma has flowed into the jar for Indra and Viṣṇu;
may it be honey-sweet for Vāyu.
These swift, tawny Soma drops have been poured forth in a stream of *ṛta*, passing through the crooked obstacles.
Strengthening Indra, crossing the waters, making all things Aryan, they strike down the stingy ones.
Pressed out, the brown drops flow along their own region toward Indra; the Soma juices go to him.
Flow with this stream, O Pavamāna, by which you caused the sun to shine,
impelling the waters of mankind.
Pavamāna has yoked Etaśa to the sun for the sake of the mind,
so that he may travel through the intermediate space.
And indeed, those ten bay horses of the Sun he has harnessed for the journey,
while the drop proclaims, "Indu is Indra!"
Pour out on every side for Vāyu the pressed juice, and for Indra the exhilarating song;
pour it through the sheep's wool filters.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us wealth that is difficult to overcome— that which is hard for the attacker to seize.
Flow toward us with thousandfold wealth consisting of cattle and horses;
flow toward us with strength and glory.
Soma, like the god Sūrya, flows purified by the stones when pressed,
placing his essence within the jar.
These bright ones, by the stream of Truth, have flowed toward the noble abodes,
bringing forth strength consisting of cattle.
The pressed Soma juices, mixed with curds, have flowed through the filter for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Soma, flow most richly in sweetness for the sake of wealth into the filter— flow as the exhilaration that is most beloved by the gods.
The Āyus cleanse him, the tawny, vigorous steed in the rivers—
the drop that exhilarates Indra.
Flow on, O Soma, bringing gold, horses, and heroic sons;
bring us strength consisting of cattle.
Pour him out for Indra, the most honey-sweet, like one seeking prize-winning strength through the sheep’s wool filter.
The inspired singers, seeking aid, purify with their prayers the Sage who is worthy of being cleansed;
bellowing like a bull, he flows onward.
With their prayers and inspired thoughts, the sages have sounded forth together the bull Soma, who crosses the waters, with the stream of *ṛta*.
Flow on, O you who are beloved by the gods; let your exhilaration go to Indra. Ascend to Vāyu according to the cosmic law.
O Pavamāna Soma, you bestow upon us wealth worthy of renown;
as one beloved, enter the ocean.
Striking down our adversaries, O Soma, you flow as the exhilarating knower of wisdom; drive away the folk who follow ungodly ways.
The purifying Soma drops, bright and radiant, have been let flow toward all poetic inspirations.
The purifying, swift, and brilliant drops have been let loose, O Indus,
striking down all enemies.
The purifying Soma-streams have been released from heaven, from the intermediate space,
and upon the ridge of the earth.
O Soma, being purified in your stream, O Indu, drive away all failures;
slay the demons, O you of noble power.
Striking down the Rākṣasas, O Soma, flow hither roaring aloud,
[bestowing] brilliant and supreme vigor.
Bestow upon us, O Soma, the treasures of heaven and those of earth; O Indu, grant us all things worthy of choice.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose ordinances are bull-like. As a bull, you uphold the sacred laws.
O Bull, your power is bull-like; you are a bull, the wood is a bull, and the exhilaration is a bull.
O Bull, truly you are a bull.
Like a neighing stallion, O *indus*, you have bellowed for the cows and for the horses;
open wide for us the doors to wealth.
The prize-winning Soma drops have been poured forth, seeking cattle and horses— bright, swift, and longing for heroes.
Being beautified by those who love the *ṛta*, and being cleansed by the hands,
they flow through the sheep's wool filter.
May those Soma juices flow for the donor, bestowing all treasures— those of heaven, those of earth, and those of the intermediate space.
O Pavamāna, knower of all things, your streams have been released like the rays of the sun.
Making a banner from heaven, you flow toward all forms;
O Soma, you swell like the ocean.
Being urged on, O Pavamāna, you send forth your voice according to the law;
you have stepped forth like the god Sūrya.
The conscious drop has been purified, dear to the sages through their hymns;
he lets loose the horse like a charioteer.
The wave that, as a seeker of the gods, has flowed around in the filter— sitting down in the womb of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
Flow for us into the filter as that exhilarating draught which most invites the gods,
O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Flow for nourishment with your stream, being purified by the wise;
O Indu, go toward the cows with your luster.
Being purified, O lover of songs, create wide space and strength for the people,
O tawny one, as you are released toward the milk-mixture.
Being purified for the feast of the gods, go to the appointed place of Indra,
shining and guided by the prize-winning steeds.
Being urged forward toward the ocean, the swift drops have been released,
impelled by the prayer.
Being cleansed, the active drops have flowed at will into the ocean,
reaching the womb of the Eternal Order.
Come around us, seeking us, with all treasures by your might;
protect us with hero-filled shelter.
The carrier Etaśa, yoking his place with the chanters,
bellows forth when he is set upon the ocean.
When the swift one settles into the golden womb of the Cosmic Order,
he leaves behind those who lack understanding.
The longing ones cry out to him; the wise desire him, while those lacking discernment sink down.
O Indu, flow most sweetly for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,
to sit upon the seat of the Truth.
The inspired poets, the wise ordainers who know the sacred word, prepare you;
the active men cleanse you thoroughly.
O Sage, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink your juice;
so do the Maruts of the one who is being purified.
O Soma, being purified, you send forth inspired speech,
O Indu, which brings a thousandfold bounty.
And so, O Soma, Indu, while being purified, bring us speech that brings a thousandfold reward and is worthy of sacrifice.
O Indu, being purified, O you who are invoked by many, enter the ocean as one beloved among these people.
With flashing luster and with swelling beauty,
the bright Soma juices, mixed with milk, flow forth.
Urged on by the impellers, the prize-winner has stepped forth toward the prize, like those sitting down as eager suitors.
O Soma, gathering together for our well-being, you, the seer from heaven, flow forth uniquely;
purify yourself so that the sun may be seen.
The radiant sisters, the kinswomen, longing for the great one, send forth the great Indu, their lord.
O Pavamāna, as a god from among the gods, with splendor after splendor,
enter into all treasures.
O Pavamāna, flow for us with excellent praise, rain, and service for the gods;
flow for continuous nourishment.
For you are a bull by your radiance; we, with pious thoughts, invoke you, O Pavamāna, the resplendent one.
Flow forth, O well-armed one, rejoicing, bestowing heroic strength; come hither, O Indu!
When you are sprinkled with waters and cleansed by the two hands,
you reach your seat upon the wooden vessel.
Sing forth for Soma Pavamāna as Vyaśva did,
for the great one who possesses a thousand eyes.
Whose honey-dropping, golden-hued color they urge forth with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Of you, the prize-winning steed who has won all riches, we choose the friendship.
Flow as a bull in your stream, O exhilarating one, for the sake of the Maruts,
bestowing all things by your might.
Thee, O Pavamāna, the sustainer of the two worlds, who beholdest the light of heaven, the winner of prizes— such as thee do I urge on in the contests for booty.
O golden one, being perceived by this inspired song, flow clear with your stream;
urge on our ally in the contests for booty.
O Indu, flow for us as one visible to all, purifying great nourishment for us; O Soma, you who find the way.
The jars have resounded with the streams of Soma by its might; O Indu, enter the vessels for Indra’s drinking.
O you whose intoxicating, sharp juice they milk out with the stones— purify yourself as the slayer of the arrogant foe.
The King, Pavamāna, is impelled by prayers of wisdom over the mind,
in order to travel through the intermediate space.
O Indu, bring to us a hundredfold increase of cattle and noble horses;
bring us fortune for our aid.
O Soma, being pressed for the feast of the gods, bring us conquering power and swiftness, like beauty for the sake of splendor.
Flow on, O Soma, most brilliant, roaring toward the wooden vats,
settling like a hawk upon its nest.
Winning the waters, Soma flows for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, the Maruts, and Viṣṇu.
Bestowing nourishment upon our offspring and upon us from every side, O Soma, flow for us with thousandfold wealth.
Those Soma juices which are pressed in the distance, those which are pressed nearby, or those which are in Śaryaṇāvat;
Those who are among the Ārjīkas, those who are among the Kṛtvas, those who are in the midst of the dwellings, or those who are among the five peoples— [may they all enjoy this Soma].
May these pressed divine drops, the Indus, flow for us from heaven with rain and with great heroic strength.
The beloved, tawny one flows, being praised by Jamadagni,
as he is urged forth upon the cowhide.
The bright drops, seeking strength and urged forward like coursers,
are purified while being mixed with the waters.
Thee, present at the pressings, they have urged forth for the service of the gods;
so flow thou with this luster.
Today we choose for you that skillful bearer who brings bliss,
the protector who is desired by many.
To the delightful one, to the excellent one, to the inspired singer, to the wise one— to the protector, to the one desired by many.
Bring wealth and gracious wisdom; O you of noble power, bring it into our bodies; bring the protector who is desired by many.
Flow on, O you who belong to all people, toward all poetic insights, as a friend to be praised by your friends.
O Soma Pavamāna, you rule over the universe through those two abodes which stand facing one another.
O Soma, you encompass all your domains on every side;
O Sage, as Pavamāna, you flow through the seasons.
Flow on, generating strengthening foods and all desirable things,
as a friend for the sake of his friends' aid.
Your bright rays, O Soma, extend across the back of heaven through your purifying filters according to your stations.
O Soma, these seven rivers flow according to your command;
for you the milch-cows run.
O Soma, flow forth in a stream when pressed for Indra as an exhilarating draught,
bestowing imperishable fame.
The seven sisters, urging you on, have together sounded forth with their prayers— the inspired sage—
at the birthplace of Vivasvat.
The active maidens cleanse you together upon the sheep’s wool, on the sounding surface,
when you, the singer, are anointed in the wood.
O Sage, O Steed, the streams of you, Pavamāna, have been released,
like coursers eager for renown.
They have been poured toward the honey-dripping vessel upon the sheep’s wool;
the prayers have lowed in response.
Toward the ocean, the drops have flowed like milch-cows to their stalls; they have entered the womb of the Eternal Order.
O Indu, flow forth for our great delight; the waters, the rivers, flow on when you clothe yourself in the milk of the cows.
In this friendship of yours, O Indu, we, desiring to sacrifice and protected by you, yearn for your companionship.
Flow on for the quest for cattle, O Soma, for the great one who beholds men;
enter into the belly of Indra.
Great art thou, O Soma, the eldest; O Indu, thou art the mightiest of the mighty.
As a warrior, thou hast ever been victorious.
He who is mightier even than the mighty, more heroic than the heroes,
and more generous even than those who give abundantly.
O Soma, you are the impeller of the sun; for the winning of offspring and for our own bodies, we choose you for friendship, we choose you for alliance.
O Agni, you purify our lives; pour forth upon us strength and nourishment. Drive misfortune far away.
Agni is the seer, the purifying one, the domestic priest of the five peoples;
we implore him for great wealth.
O Agni, you who are skillful in your work, purify yourself for us; bestowing upon me splendor, heroic strength, wealth, and nourishment.
Pavamāna flows across all obstacles toward our fair praise,
visible to all like the sun.
Being cleansed by the Āyus, full of nourishment and placed for our enjoyment, Indu, the far-seeing steed, flows onward.
Pavamāna has generated the lofty *ṛta*, the bright light;
he has struck down the black darknesses.
As the tawny Pavamāna strikes down [the obstacles], his bright drops have been released— swift and possessing restless luster.
Pavamāna, the best of charioteers, most brilliantly praised with his brilliant [rays],
is golden-hued and accompanied by the host of Maruts.
Pavamāna, the best winner of booty, has pervaded [the world] with his rays,
bestowing heroic strength upon the singer.
Being pressed, the Indu has flowed forth across the sheep’s-wool filter; being purified, the Indu flows toward Indra.
This Soma, pressed by the stones, sports upon the skin of the cows;
he loudly calls Indra for exhilaration.
O Pavamāna, with that radiant milk of yours which has been brought down from heaven, be gracious to us so that we may live.
O Soma, you are the sustainer, the delightful and most powerful at the sacrifice;
flow on, bestowing abundant wealth.
Pressed out for Indra, you are the exhilarating one who gladdens men; as a wise patron, you flow with your juice as the most intoxicating.
Pressed by the stones, flow forth with a roar;
pour out brilliant strength, the highest power.
The drop, being urged forward, flows through the woollen filters;
the tawny one has bellowed for the prize of victory.
O Indu, you flow through the sheep's wool, spreading fame, spreading good fortune,
and spreading strengths rich in cattle, O Soma.
O Indu, bring us wealth consisting of hundreds, cattle, and horses;
O Soma, bring it in thousands.
The purifying drops, the swift Indus, have passed through the filter and reached Indra on their courses.
The preeminent, Soma-like juice, the drop, ancient for Indra— life itself, it purifies itself for the living one.
The dawns urge on the hero, the purifying one who drips with sweetness;
they have sounded forth together with their song.
May Pūṣan, whose horses are goats, be our protector on every journey;
may he grant us a share among the maidens.
This Soma flows like honeyed ghee for the one with matted hair;
may he grant us a share among the maidens.
O glowing one, this pressed juice of yours flows pure like clarified butter;
may it find enjoyment among our maidens.
O Soma, as the progenitor of the speech of sages, flow clear with your stream;
you are the bestower of treasures among the gods.
The falcon rushes toward the jars; he plunges into his armor, crying out loudly toward the wooden vats.
O Soma, your pressed juice has been poured forth all around into the jar;
like a darting hawk, it flows onward.
Flow clear, O Soma, exhilarating for Indra, as the most honey-sweet.
They have been let loose for the feast of the gods, like chariots seeking booty.
These pressed juices, most intoxicating and bright, have been released toward Vāyu.
Pressed by the stone and extolled, O Soma, you go to the filter,
bestowing heroic vigor upon the singer.
This one, pressed and praised, plunges through the filter,
the slayer of demons, into the sheep’s wool.
Whatever fear finds me here, whether it be near or far away— O Pavamāna, strike that down!
May that Pavamāna, the all-seeing one, purify us today with the filter—he who is the Purifier; may he cleanse us.
O Agni, with that purifier of yours which is spread within your flame, purify our sacred prayer (*brahman*).
O Agni, with that radiant purifier of yours, purify us;
with the inspirations of sacred prayer, purify us.
O God Savitṛ, with both— by means of the purifier and by your impulse—
purify me on every side.
O God Savitṛ, O Soma, with three most excellent abodes,
and with skillful powers, O Agni, purify us.
May the divine folk purify me; may the Vasus purify me with their wisdom. O All-Gods, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me.
Swell forth, flow onward, O Soma, with all your stalks—
the most excellent oblation for the gods.
We have come, bearing homage, to the beloved youth who bestows gifts, who is strengthened by oblations.
The axe of Alāyya has been destroyed; O divine Soma, flow for him, even as for a mere mouse, O divine Soma.
He who studies the Pāvamānī verses— the essence gathered by the seers—
consumes everything purified and made savory by Mātariśvan.
Whoever studies the Pāvamānī hymns— the essence gathered by the seers—
for him Sarasvatī milks forth milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
Toward the god, the honeyed drops have flowed forth like milch-cows toward their calves.
Seated upon the sacred grass (*barhis*), eloquent with their voices, they have taken the *parisrut* liquor as their udders and the milk of the ruddy cow as their robe.

Roaring loudly, he has bellowed toward the earlier [vessels]; loosening the heights, the tawny one is sweetened. Passing through the filter into the wide expanse, the god deposits his own shoots according to his will.

The exhilaration that has measured out the two meeting sisters, who increase together, swells the imperishable waters with milk. Spreading through the two great, boundless regions, he has assumed an exhaustible luster as he moves forward.
Moving between his two parents, seeking strength, the wise one makes his station swell with his own inherent power.
The stalk is adorned with barley; led by the men, he unites with his kinsmen and protects his head.
The sage is born with a skillful mind; he is the hidden germ of Cosmic Order, placed beyond the twins.
Being young, they two first brought forth that which was hidden in the cave—the birth not yet arisen.
The wise have discerned the form of the delightful one, when the falcon brought the plant from afar.
They purified him, the well-increasing, the yearning stalk, as he moved through the rivers—the one who encompasses all and is worthy of song.
O Soma, the ten young women cleanse you, the pressed one, who have been prepared by the seers with prayers and meditations;
through the fleece-strainers and the invocations of the gods, directed by the men, you burst forth for the winning of booty.
The inspired hymns and chants have celebrated Soma as he flows forth— the one worthy of praise, who sits with the well-disposed,
the immortal winner of wealth who, from heaven, sends forth his voice with a honeyed wave in a stream.
This Soma, being purified, sends forth everything from heaven; he settles in the jars throughout the entire mid-air.
Pressed by the stones, he is cleansed with water and milk; as Indu is purified, may he find dear and wide space.
Thus, O Soma, being poured out for us, flow on, bestowing most wondrous vitality.
We invoke the benevolent Heaven and Earth; O gods, grant us wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
Like an arrow set upon the bow, the prayer is aimed; like a calf let loose to the mother’s udder, it flows forth.
Like a wide-streaming cow, she yields at the beginning as she approaches; Soma is impelled within his sacred ordinances.
The prayer is joined; the honey is poured; the sweet-toned tongue is urged within the mouth.
Pavamāna, like a continuous stream of those who strike, flows as a honeyed drop through the filter.
Desiring a bride, he flows through the sheep’s wool and over the skin; the granddaughter of Aditi loosens her bonds for him who goes toward the *ṛta*.
The golden-hued, worshipful, well-restrained exhilaration has stepped forth; sharpening his manly powers, he shines like a buffalo.

The bull bellows; the milch-cows approach him; the goddesses go to the appointed place of the god. Soma has passed through the white sheep’s wool; he has clothed himself in a garment as if it were newly washed.

Clad in an unsoiled, radiant garment, the golden-hued immortal one puts on his bright raiment; with power he has fashioned the back of heaven as a covering for his adornment, a cloud-like carpet for the two vessels.
Like the rays of the sun, the exhilarating, sleep-inducing drops rush forth together as they flow.
Like swift streams around a stretched-out thread, no station whatsoever flows clear except for Indra.
Like swift waters on a downward slope toward the sea, the exhilarating draughts poured by the Bull have found their course.
May there be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds in our dwelling; O Soma, may strengths and the people abide with us.
Flow for us with wealth, with gold, with horses, with cattle, with barley, and with great heroic strength.
For you, O Soma, are my fathers; you are the heads of heaven, established as the makers of vitality.
These Soma drops, being purified, have sped forth toward Indra like chariots for the sake of booty;
pressed out, they pass through the sheep’s-wool filter, casting off their golden covering as they flow toward the rain.
O Indu, flow clear for the great Indra, as one who is very gracious, blameless, and a destroyer of enemies.
Bring splendid treasures to the one who praises you; O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
Three times seven milch-cows have milked for him the true *āśīr* in the ancient sky;
he has made four other beautiful worlds for his adornment when he grew strong through the cosmic laws (*ṛta*).
Seeking the lovely nectar of immortality, he has separated both heaven and earth by his poetic wisdom (*kāvyena*).
With majesty, he has clothed himself in the most brilliant waters when they, through the glory of the god, have found their seat.
May those rays of his be immortal and invincible, following both generations—
those by which they purify both human and divine powers, and then they seized him, the king, with their thoughts.
Being cleansed by the ten skillful workers, he is present among the middle mothers;
guarding the laws of the lovely nectar, he who beholds men looks upon both races.
Being cleansed for the sake of providing Indra’s power, he, established between both ends of heaven and earth, exults.
As a bull, with his vigor, he drives away the malevolent ones, pointing toward the spoils like an archer aiming at his targets.
Like a young bull beholding his two mothers, he goes bellowing like the roar of the Maruts;
knowing the primordial *ṛta*, the one of noble will chose the sun-dweller for his praise.

The terrible bull bellows with great power, the far-seeing one sharpening his golden horns. Soma settles into his well-fashioned seat; the cowhide becomes his garment, and the sheep’s wool his mantle.
Pure, purifying his own stainless body, the tawny one has flowed down onto the back of the sheep’s wool.
Pleasing to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the honeyed juice is prepared in three ways by the skillful workers.
Flow clear, O Soma, for the banquet of the gods; enter the heart of Indra, the vessel that holds the Soma.
Before distress can overcome us, carry us across all misfortune; for as one who knows the land, he points out the directions to the one who asks.
Like a well-harnessed steed toward the prize, flow on; O Indu, purify yourself into the belly of Indra.
Like one skilled in crossing a river by boat, carry us across; like a hero fighting in battle, protect us from reproach.
The sacrificial fee is bestowed; the vigorous one seeks his seat. Watchful, he guards against the malicious demon.
The tawny one makes the head-band, the milk of the clouds; he spreads it as a cushion for the two bowls, and the sacred prayer serves as his robe.
Like a ploughman for his field, he goes forth bellowing with strength; he casts off that asuric hue of his.
He leaves behind the covering of his father, goes to his own appointed place, and continually makes for himself a shimmering garment.
Pressed by the stones, he flows from the hands; he acts like a bull with the cloud and is stirred by the hymn.
He rejoices, he approaches, he accomplishes his task through song; he cleanses himself in the waters and worships at the boundary of the rite.
They pour out the celestial draught of honey from the dwelling, which increases the mountain by its power and overcomes all;
in which the cows, eaters of well-offered oblations, mix the foremost essence at their udder with their vast expanses.
The ten sisters have sent him forth together from the two arms, like a chariot, into the lap of Aditi.
He has gone and he hastens toward the secret place of the cow, which his inspired thoughts have brought into being.

Like a hawk to its nest, the god hastens to sit upon the golden seat prepared by prayer; they lead him, beloved, with song onto the sacred grass; like a horse, he, worthy of sacrifice, goes unto the gods.
The ruddy seer of heaven has appeared; the bull with three backs has lowed toward the cows. With a thousandfold guidance, moving hither and thither, he shines through many dawns like a singer.
He assumes a brilliant form; his color is such that wherever he rests, he drives away those who cause failure.
Winning the waters, he goes by his own power to the divine folk; he unites with our fair praise, with that which is led by cattle.
Like a bull bellowing as he circles the herds, he has assumed the splendors of the sun.
The divine eagle has looked down upon the earth; Soma beholds all creatures with his wisdom.
They cleanse the tawny one; he is yoked like a ruddy steed; Soma is mixed with milk-streams in the jar.
He sends forth his voice; they urge him on with hymns—how many dear friends there are of him who is praised by many!
Many wise men speak together when they have poured the Soma into Indra’s belly;
when the men with skillful hands cleanse the desirable honey with the ten sisters who share a common nest.
Not resting, he passes beyond the cows, across the dear lowing of Sūrya’s daughter. To him Vinangṛsa brought what was pleasing; he dwells together with his twin sisters, his consorts.
Shaken by men, pressed by stones upon the sacred grass, the beloved lord of kine from of old, the seasonal drop— endowed with wisdom,
the accomplisher of man’s sacrifice, pure through meditation— O Indra, the Soma flows for you.

Urged by the arms of men, the pressed Soma flows for you, O Indra, in a stream according to its nature. You have fulfilled our intentions; you have gathered our thoughts at the sacrifice. Like a bird alighting on a tree, the tawny one has settled within the two bowls.
The skillful and wise poets milk the thundering, inexhaustible stalk, the Seer;
the cows and the hymns, being reborn, come together in unison at the seat of the womb of Cosmic Order.
At the navel of the earth, the supporter of the great heaven, nourished within the waves of the waters and the rivers—
the thunderbolt of Indra, the bull, the possessor of abundant wealth— Soma flows clear for the heart, the delightful exhilarator.
Flow then, O wise one, around the earthly realm, bestowing gifts upon the singer and the one who shakes the ladle.
Do not exclude us from the wealth that touches our dwelling; may we clothe ourselves in abundant, golden-hued riches.
O Indu, bring to us a hundredfold gift of horses, a thousandfold gift of cattle and gold!
Bestow upon us great and wealthy nourishments; O Pavamāna, come to our hymn of praise.
At the snout of the blowing drop, they have sounded together; in the womb of the Eternal Law (Ṛta), the centers have come together.
That Asura has made three heads for himself to grasp; the ships of Truth have carried the well-doer across.
Moving perfectly together, the mighty ones have rushed forth; upon the wave of the river, the seekers have stirred themselves.
Generating the hymn with streams of honey, they have increased the dear body of Indra.
Wielding the filter, they sit around the speech; their ancient father guards their sacred law.
Varuṇa has veiled himself within the great ocean; only the wise have been able to grasp him in his foundations.
In the thousand-streamed [soma], they have sounded together like [the waters] in the vault of heaven; the honey-tongued ones flow unceasingly.
His watchful spies do not close their eyes; at every step there are bridgers who bear nooses.
