Those who have resounded from their father and mother, shining with the *ṛc* and consuming the lawless,
blow away by their creative power (*māyā*) the black skin hated by Indra, from the earth and from the heavens.

Those who have sounded forth from the ancient measure, the controllers of the hymn, the thinkers of the impetuous one—the blind and the deaf have perished; the doers of evil do not cross the path of *ṛta*.
Upon the outspread filter with its thousand streams, the wise seers purify their speech.
Of these, the Rudras are vigorous and guileless; they are swift-moving spies, fair to behold, and watchers over men.
Guardian of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), he who is of noble intellect cannot be deceived; he has placed three purifiers within his heart.
Knowing all, he beholds all beings; he pierces those who lack devotion and casts the lawless into the pit.
The thread of Cosmic Order is stretched across the filter by the power of Varuṇa’s magic upon the tip of the tongue.
Even the wise reach for it and attain it; there the powerless one falls away from the work.
Like a newborn infant, he bellows in the wood when the ruddy prize-winning steed seeks to win the light of heaven.
He accompanies the seed of heaven, which increases with milk; him we implore for his favor and for wide-reaching protection.

He who is the pillar of heaven, its support, well-spread out—the full stalk moves all around. May he, the Seer, worship these two great worlds with his rites; the Sage has established them together and has gathered all nourishments.
Great is the refreshing draught, well-prepared and sweet with Soma; vast is the pasture for him who follows the Law of Aditi.
He who rules over the rain from here, the ruddy bull, the leader of the waters, he who comes hither, the worthy of praise.
The vitalized cloud is milked for ghee and milk; the navel of Cosmic Order produces the immortal.
Facing one another, the bounteous ones gratify him; the men, the pourers, release what is beneficial.
The stalk has roared, accompanied by its wave; it swells the skin that is dear to the gods for the sake of man.
It places the germ in the lap of Aditi, by which we may obtain both offspring and descendants.

Like those that flow in a thousand streams, may they be inexhaustible and rich in progeny in the third realm. The four navels, established from beneath the sky, bring the immortal oblation, dripping with clarified butter.

When he desires to win, Soma assumes a white form; the bountiful Asura knows the full extent of the world. Through prayer and ritual labor he accompanies the sacrifice; may he burst open the water-holding cask from heaven.
Then the prize-winning steed, having won, has stepped upon the white vessel anointed with milk at the place of the goal;
the god-seeking ones have urged him on with their minds for Kakṣīvat, who has lived a hundred winters, [giving] hundreds of cows.
O Soma, as your juice is blended with the waters, it flows through the sheep’s wool filter, O Pavamāna.
Being cleansed by the sages, O most intoxicating one, become sweet for Indra to drink, O Pavamāna.
The youthful one, well-disposed toward us, purifies himself for his dear names, upon which he grows great;
the far-seeing and lofty one has mounted the wide-reaching chariot of the lofty Sūrya.
The tongue of Order flows as the beloved honey; the speaker, the lord of this prayer, is inviolable. As a son, he bestows upon his parents their secret third name in the luminous realm of heaven.
Shining forth, he has bellowed toward the jars; guided by the men, he is in the golden vessel.
The milch-cows of Truth have lowed unto him; the three-backed one shines across the dawns.
Pressed by the stones and made pleasing by the prayers, the pure one, illuminating both parents, Heaven and Earth, flows through the sheep’s woolly fleece; a stream of honey, swelling day by day.
O Soma, flow forth for our well-being; being purified by the men, clothe yourself in the milk-mixture.
With those exhilarating, far-reaching intoxications of yours, impel Indra to bestow wealth upon us.
The sustainer of heaven, the effective essence, the skill of the gods, he flows clear, to be celebrated by men.
Released like a tawny steed by warriors, he spreads his splendors at will across the rivers.
Like a hero, he takes up weapons in his hands, desiring to win the light of heaven as a charioteer in the quests for cattle.
Stirring up the vigor of Indra with his active works, the Indu, being urged forward, is anointed by the wise.

O Soma Pavamāna, entering Indra’s bellies with your wave while increasing his strength, swell out for us like lightning from the cloud, filling both worlds; through our prayer, mete out for us eternal spoils of war.
The King of all, who beholds the light of heaven, flows clear; he, the conqueror of seers, has caused the thought of *ṛta* to resound.
He who is cleansed by the ray of the sun, the father of prayers, whose wisdom is unattainable.
Like a bull toward the herds, you flow around the vat, bellowing as a bull in the lap of the waters.
As the most intoxicating one, you purify yourself for Indra, so that we may conquer in battle through your aid.
This honeyed one has bellowed forth into the vat; Indra’s thunderbolt, more beautiful than the beautiful.
Toward him flow the well-milking, ghee-dropping streams of Truth, like lowing cows with their milk.
That ancient one flows forth, whom the hawk, dispatched from heaven, churned out across the mid-air;
trembling with fear at the mind of the archer Kr̥śānu, he takes up the honeyed juice.
May those former and later drops flow for us toward great wealth consisting of cattle— those lovely ones,
like serpents, worthy of being beheld, who have delighted in every prayer and every oblation.
May this Indu, the wise one praised by many with a focused mind, conquer those who attack us;
he who, at the seat of the Lord, has taken his place as the embryo, now flows toward the wide-open stall of the cows.
The active, potent juice, the maker of heaven, flows clear; he is the great, undeceived Varuṇa for the one who goes astray.
Mitra has been pressed out, worthy of sacrifice among the tribes, bellowing like a stallion seeking mares within the herd.
The King, generating speech, has flowed forth; clothing himself in the waters, he desires the cows.
The fleece of the sheep retains his impurity; purified, he goes to the appointed place of the gods.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra by the men; you, the wave, the seer who beholds men, are anointed in the wood.
For many are your paths to travel, and a thousand bay horses are seated in the vessels.
The Apsarases of the ocean, sitting within, have flowed toward the wise Soma;
they urge him on, the conqueror of the stronghold, and beg the purifying one for imperishable bliss.
Winning cattle for us, winning chariots, winning gold, winning the light, winning waters, winning thousands, Soma flows clear—
he whom the gods have made into a draught for drinking, the sweetest drop, ruddy, and a source of bliss.
O Soma Pavamāna, favoring us, making these true riches manifest, you flow onward.
Slay the enemy both near and far; grant us wide pastures and security.
May our unimpelled drops flow forth, the tawny ones pressed out for those of lofty heaven.
May the hostilities of the enemy depart from us; may they perish, and may our prayers win the prize.
May the Soma drops flow forth for us, distilling exhilaration, or those riches by which we urge on our steeds.
Beyond the encompassing reach of any mortal, may we always carry away spoils of wealth.
For he is an enemy through his own ill-will, and he is a wolf through the ill-will of another.
Like thirst in the desert, let him be overcome; O Soma Pavamāna, strike down those of evil intent.
In heaven, at your navel, is that which is supreme; upon the ridge of the earth, your shoots have grown.
The pressing-stones chew you upon the ox-hide; with their hands, the wise have milked you from the waters.
Thus, O Indu, the first preparers press out for you your well-formed, beautifully adorned juice.
O Pavamāna, overcome every adversary; let your power be manifest, your exhilarating draught beloved.

The stream of Soma, who beholds men, flows clear; by the Eternal Law, he calls the gods from heaven. O Bṛhaspati, he flashes forth with thunderous roar; like oceans, they have encompassed the libations.
O vigorous one, you whom the cows have lowed toward as you ascend the iron-fashioned womb, resplendent;
prolonging the life of the patrons and their great glory, O Soma, you flow as a bull, a rapturous exhilarant for Indra.
The most intoxicating one flows into the belly of Indra, clothing himself in strength for the sake of glory, most auspicious.
He has extended himself toward all beings; playing, the tawny, virile steed flows onward.
The men, the ten fingers, milk you out for the gods—the most honey-sweet one with a thousand streams.
O Soma, set in motion by the men and pressed by the stones, as a conqueror of thousands, flow for all the gods.
The ten fingers milk you, the bull, rich in sweetness, with stones in the waters;
O Soma, exhilarating Indra and the divine host, you flow as Pavamāna like a wave from the ocean.
The well-adorned waves of the purifying Soma go forth into the belly of Indra.
When the pressed juices, mixed with the glorious curd of cows, have been drawn up, they have exhilarated the Hero for the giving of gifts.
For Soma has flowed toward the jars like a stallion, a steed with swift-moving tracks;
he, the bull, knowing both lineages of the gods, attains that which exists from yonder and from here.
O Soma Pavamāna, scatter wealth upon us; O Indu, be a bountiful giver of great riches. Bestow strength upon the liberal patron with your gracious wisdom; do not pour away our household far from us.
May Pūṣan, Pavamāna, and the bounteous Mitra come to us, as well as Varuṇa with his companions;
may Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Vāyu, the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, and the well-guiding Sarasvatī [come].
Both Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, the god Aryaman,
Aditi, the Ordainer, Bhaga, the protector of men, the wide mid-air, and all the gods— may they take pleasure in Pavamāna.
The ruddy, tawny Soma has been pressed; like a wondrous king, he has bellowed toward the cows.
Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep’s wool filter to sit, like a hawk, upon his ghee-filled nest.
As a sage, you move around the greatness of the ordainer; like a groomed steed, you flow toward the prize.
Warding off misfortunes, O Soma, be gracious; clothed in clarity, you go around your radiant garment.
Parjanya is the father of the great-winged bird; at the navel of the earth, he has established his dwelling among the mountains.
The waters, his sisters, have flowed toward the cows; he unites with the pressing-stones when the sacrifice is prepared.
Like a wife to her husband, you bestow your favor; O child of Pajrā, listen, for I speak to you.
Enter among the songs so that we may live well; blameless, O Soma, remain watchful in the assembly.
As for the ancients, O Indu, you have brought us wealth—winning hundreds, winning thousands, bringing booty in your course;
even so, flow on for new prosperity, for the waters follow your law.
O Brahmaṇaspati, your purifier is spread out; as its master, you encompass all your limbs from every side.
One whose body has not been heated by austerity, being raw, does not attain that [state]; only those who have been cooked [by fire] and carry it [the offering] reach it together.
The filter of the heating [Soma] is stretched out at the station of heaven; its glowing threads have spread abroad.
The swift ones protect its purifier; with their mind, they stand upon the back of heaven.
The dappled, foremost bull has caused the dawns to shine; seeking strength, he sustains all beings.
By his creative power, the masters of illusion have measured him out; the fathers, who behold men, have deposited the germ.
The Gandharva thus guards his station; the wondrous one protects the generations of the gods.
As the lord of the treasure, he seizes the enemy with his snare; those who have performed most excellent deeds have partaken of the draught of honey.

O possessor of the oblation, clothed in the celestial cloud, you go around the sacrifice to the great divine seat. King whose chariot is the filter, you have mounted for the prize; with a thousand points, you win lofty fame.
Flow on as the exhilarating drink, O most active one, winning the waters for Indra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu. Grant us today wide space and well-being; in this broad dwelling, celebrate the divine host.
The immortal Soma flows around all those worlds upon which he has taken his stand;
effecting both union and separation for our aid, Indu follows after them as the sun follows the dawn.
He who is poured out with milk among the plants, seeking the favor of the gods and bringing wealth;
pressed with the lightning-flash in a stream, Soma flows for Indra, exhilarating the divine host.
This very Soma flows clear, the winner of thousands, strengthening the vigorous voice that awakens at dawn.
The drop, with the winds, raises up the ocean; he settles in the jars within the heart of Indra.

The cows blend that Soma with milk—the increaser of milk—who finds the light of heaven through their prayers. The winner of wealth, the effective juice, flows clear; he is the inspired sage, the seer, worthy of praise through his poetic wisdom.
O Soma, well-pressed for Indra, flow forth; let disease depart along with the demons.
Let not the double-dealing ones delight in your juice; here let the drops be full of wealth.

O Pavamāna, urge us forward in the battle; for you are the skillful, beloved exhilaration of the gods. Slay the enemies who raise their shouts against us; drink the soma, O Indra, and strike down our adversaries.
O Indu, inviolable and most intoxicating, you flow clear; you become the supreme nourishment for Indra’s self.
Many wise ones sing toward you; they honor the king of this world.
With a thousand hymns and a hundred streams, the wondrous Indu flows as desirable honey for Indra.
Winning the field, flow toward us; winning the waters, O bounteous Soma, make wide for us a path to go.
Roaring, you are anointed with milk in the jar; you flow through the sheep’s woolen filter. Being cleansed like a prize-winning steed, O Soma, you have flowed into the belly of Indra.
Flow sweet for the divine race; flow sweet for Indra, whose name is easy to invoke.
Flow sweet, honeyed, and invincible for Mitra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati.
The ten fingers cleanse the steed in the jar; the inspired thoughts and voices of the sages surge forward.
The purifying drops flow toward the hymn of praise; the intoxicating Soma-drops enter into Indra.
Pavamāna, flow toward us with heroic strength, a wide pasture, and great, far-reaching protection.
Let no one’s hostility have power over us; O Indu, may we conquer every prize through you.
The far-seeing bull has mounted the sky; the sage has illuminated the luminous realms of heaven.
The king, bellowing, passes through the filter; those who watch over men milk the nectar of heaven.
In the vault of heaven, the honey-tongued, tireless seers milk the mountain-dwelling bull;
they milk the drop that has grown great in the waters, the honey-sweet one in the ocean's wave, within the filter.
Many songs of longing have yearned for the fair-winged one who has flown up to the firmament;
the prayers lick the infant, the golden bird who stands upon the earth, the one who is worthy of praise.
The Gandharva has stood erect upon the vault of heaven, beholding all the forms of this [world].
His radiance has shone forth with bright luster; pure, he has illuminated both worlds, the two parents.
O Pavamāna, your swift, exhilarating drops, urged by prayer, flow forth of their own accord like the offspring of fleet-footed mares.
Like divine, well-winged birds, the honey-sweet, most intoxicating drops settle within the vessel.
Your exhilarating, intoxicating, and swift draughts have been poured forth like chariot-horses racing apart.
Like a cow with her milk for her calf, the honeyed waves of soma-drops flow toward Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Like a steed urged forward toward the prize, flow toward the light-winning vat, the mother rock of heaven.
A bull upon the woolly surface of the filter, Soma is purified for the sake of bestowing Indra’s power.
O Pavamāna, your steeds, swift as horses, impelled by prayer, have been released toward heaven with their milk in the firm foundation.
The ancient seers have poured forth the inner waters, those wise ones who, O you who are the strength of the seers, cleanse you.

O all-seeing one, your rays go forth from you, the skillful and sovereign lord, encompassing all domains. Pervading with your laws, O Soma, you purify yourself; as the lord of the entire world, you reign.
On both sides, the rays of the purifying Soma—though he is constant—go forth as his banners;
when the tawny one is cleansed upon the filter, he sits as a guest in his place within the jars.
The banner of the sacrifice, the one who makes the rite successful, Soma flows; he goes to the appointed place of the gods.
With a thousand streams he rushes around the vessel; as a bull, bellowing loudly, he passes through the filter.
The King plunges into the ocean; the rivers follow his wave as he rests within the streams.
Purifying himself, he has mounted the woolly back upon the navel of the earth, the sustainer of the great heaven.
Roaring like the ridge of heaven, he has bellowed—he by whose laws both heaven and earth abide.
Discerning the friendship of Indra, Soma flows clear; being purified, he settles within the jars.
The light of the sacrifice, the beloved honey, flows clear; the father of the gods, their progenitor, the possessor of abundant wealth.
He bestows the secret treasure within the two self-sustaining worlds—the most intoxicating, exhilarating, and Indra-like juice.
Crying out, the vigorous steed flows toward the jar; the far-seeing Lord of Heaven with a hundred streams;
the tawny bull, being cleansed by the sheep’s wool and the rivers, settles in the dwelling places of Mitra.

Pavamāna flows at the head of the rivers; as the foremost one, he goes at the head of speech toward the cattle. He shares in the great prize of booty at the head; well-armed, the bull is purified by the pressers.
This Pavamāna, like a bird that has alighted, has sped with his wave through the woollen fleece;
by your power, O Sage, between the two worlds, the pure Soma flows with prayer for you, O Indra.

Clothed in his mantle that touches the heavens, the worshipful one, filling the mid-air, is established among the worlds. Born from the light, he has stepped forth with the mist; he seeks to win over his ancient father.
He bestows great protection upon his people, he who has pervaded his first abode;
from that station of his which is in the highest heaven, he comes together with all the gathered hosts.

The drop has gone forth to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not violate the agreement with his friend. Like a youth with young women, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred courses.
Your exhilarating, praising, and glorious thoughts have stepped forth to the communal gatherings.
With inspired hymns, the chants have celebrated Soma; the milch-cows have poured forth their milk.
O Soma, O Indu, as you are being purified, flow for us with continuous, swelling, and unfailing nourishment—
that inexhaustible milk which yields for us thrice a day, providing food, strength, sweetness, and heroic power.
The bull of hymns, far-seeing Soma, flows on, the furtherer of the day, the dawn, and the sky.
By his action he has caused the rivers and the jars to resound, entering the heart of Indra through the wise ones.
The ancient sage is purified by the wise; guided by men, he has bellowed around the vessels.
Bringing forth the name of Trita, may he flow with honey so that Indra and Vāyu may perform their friendship.

Being purified, he has caused the dawns to shine; he has become the maker of space for the rivers. This Soma, milking the thrice-seven [streams] as the milk-mixture, flows for the heart—beautiful and exhilarating.

Flow on, O Soma, into the celestial abodes; being released, O Indu, flow through the filter into the jar. Seated within the belly of Indra while bellowing, guided by the men, you caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Pressed by the stones, you flow through the filter, O Indu, entering the bellies of Indra.
You became the one who looks upon men, O far-seeing Soma; you opened the cow-pen for the Aṅgirases.
O Soma, while you were being purified, the sages, seeking aid and devoted to sacred study, rejoiced after you;
O Indu, the fair-winged bird brought you down from heaven, you who are adorned by all our hymns of praise.
As he is purified with his wave in the sheep’s woolly filter, the seven milch-cows low toward the golden-hued one.
In the lap of the waters, above the womb of *ṛta*, the living ones, the mighty bulls, have impelled the Seer.
Being purified, Indu plunges past all adversaries, making all paths easy for the sacrificer;
making the cows his garment, the lovely sage flows like a playful horse through the woolen filter.
The inexhaustible, hundred-streamed, glorious waters low toward the golden one like cows seeking water;
the swift fingers cleanse him who is enveloped in milk, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.
These creatures of yours belong to the divine seed; you rule over the entire world.
And all this, O Pavamāna, is under your control; you, O Indu, are the first establisher of the sacred abodes.
You are the ocean, O Sage, the knower of all; yours are these five directions within the cosmic order.
You have surpassed both heaven and earth; yours, O Pavamāna, are the lights, including the sun.
O Soma Pavamāna, you are purified in the filter within the supporting space for the sake of the gods;
the Uśij first took hold of you, and all these worlds have submitted themselves to you.
The singer goes forth across the sheep’s wool filter; the tawny bull, the golden-hued one, has bellowed down into the wooden vessels.
The prayers have lowed together in longing; the hymns lick the infant who is worthy of praise.
He has clothed himself in the rays of the sun, weaving the triple-stranded thread as he knows how;
leading the most recent instructions of the Eternal Order, the husband of the wives goes to the appointed place.
The king of rivers flows on, the lord of heaven; he goes along the paths of *ṛta* with a loud roar.
The golden one is poured out in a thousand streams; purifying himself, generating speech, he approaches us with wealth.

O Pavamāna, you flow through the great flood like the brilliant sun through the sheep’s wool with your filter; purified by the hands and pressed by the men with the stones, you hasten toward great, prize-winning booty.
O Pavamāna, you flow toward nourishment and vigor; like a hawk among trees, you settle in the jars.
Pressed for Indra as a gladdening, intoxicating draught, you are the highest pillar of heaven, far-seeing.
The seven sisters, the mothers, [attend] the newborn infant, the noble and wise one;
for the sake of sovereignty over the entire world, they attend Soma, the divine Gandharva of the waters, who beholds men.
As Lord, you traverse these worlds, O Indu, yoking your bay, well-winged mares.
May they pour forth for you honeyed ghee and milk; O Soma, may the people abide under your law.
O Soma, you are the beholder of men on every side; O Pavamāna, O Bull, you flow through these [worlds].
As such, flow for us with wealth and gold; may we be among the beings that we may live.
O Indu, finder of cattle, finder of wealth, finder of gold, bestower of seed, established among the worlds—flow on!
O Soma, you are a hero of noble lineage and all-knowing; as such, the sages sit around you with their songs.
The wave of honey has caused the desires to stand firm; clothed in the waters, the buffalo plunges in.
The King, whose chariot is the filter, has mounted for booty; with a thousand points, he wins lofty fame.
He, the life of all, raises up on every day all auspicious, well-nourished, and offspring-bearing blessings.
O Indu, once you are drunk, entreat Indra for us to grant us sacred prayer, wealth consisting of offspring, and a household full of horses.

At the beginning of days, the tawny, desirable exhilaration is made conscious by the conscious one through the days; driving the two peoples apart, he moves between them—the human and the divine praise—within the Sustainer.
They anoint him, they anoint him apart, they anoint him together; they lick his creative power, they anoint him with honey.
As he flies at the swelling of the river, those who purify with gold seize the bull, the sacrificial animal, among these [waters].
Sing forth to the wise Pavamāna; like a great stream, the Soma-juice flows.
Like a serpent gliding over its slough, the tawny bull has flowed like a playful steed.

The leader, the king of waters, grows mighty; the measurer of days, established among the worlds. Tawny, dripping with clarity, beautiful to behold, a surging sea whose chariot is light, he flows as the one who dwells in wealth.
The supporting pillar of heaven has been released; the exhilarating draught flows around the threefold worlds.
The hymns lick the stalk that is worthy of praise, when the singers have approached it with song as its radiant garment.
Your streams, as you are purified, flow forth with speed past the fine wool of the sheep;
when, O *indu*, you are mixed with milk in the two bowls, being pressed, O Soma, you settle in the jars.
Flow clear, O Soma, winner of wisdom, worthy of our hymns; run through the sheep’s wool, bringing your beloved honey.
Strike down all the Rākṣasas and the devouring Atris, O Indu! May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Flow forth; settle within the vessel. Being purified by the men, rush toward the prize.
Cleansing you like a spirited horse, they lead you with reins toward the sacred grass.
Well-armed, the divine Indu flows clear, slaying the curse and guarding the community;
he is the father of the gods, their progenitor, most skillful, the pillar of heaven, and the support of the earth.
The seer, the inspired singer, the leader of the people, the skillful and wise Uśanas by his poetic insight—
he indeed discovered that which was deposited among them, the secret and hidden name of the cows.
This very honeyed Soma of yours, O Indra, a bull for the bull, has flowed through the filter;
winning thousands, winning hundreds, a giver of much, the prize-winning steed has taken his place upon the sacred grass for all time.
These Soma drops, seeking cattle by the thousands, for great strength and for immortality, have been released through the filters— these purifying juices, like fame-seeking steeds rushing to battle.
For he, invoked by many, being purified, has indeed flowed around all the nourishments of the people.
Now, O you who are borne by the falcon, bring us food; bestowing wealth, flow toward the prize of victory.
This Soma, being pressed, has run through the filter like a released steed;
whetting his horns like a buffalo, he rushes toward the cows like a hero seeking cattle.
This one has come forth from within the highest mountain; being somewhere, she has found the cows in the wide space.
Like lightning from heaven thundering with the clouds, O Indra, this stream of Soma flows clear for you.

And indeed, O Soma, being purified, you travel around the herd of cattle on the same chariot with Indra. O giver of life, bestower of power, grant us many great nourishments; those things are praised by you.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; for you it flows clear; drink of this!
For you indeed have you made, for you have you chosen, the drop, the Soma, for the fitting exhilaration.
Like a chariot that conquers many, he has been harnessed for the winning of great and manifold treasures.
Then all the human races and the trees have raised themselves on high to sing his praise at the winning of the light.
Like Vāyu with his team of horses, you whose path is swift; like the Nāsatyas at our invocation, you are most beneficent.
O Soma, you are all-desirable, like Draviṇodas in person, and like Pūṣan, you are the impeller of our thoughts.
Like Indra, you who have performed great deeds, you are the slayer of Vṛtras, O Soma, the breaker of forts;
for like the steed of Pedu, you are the slayer of those called "serpents," O Soma, and the destroyer of every Dasyu.
Like Agni cast upon the forest, he who freely displays his splendors in the rivers;
like a warrior facing the great foe, Soma Pavamāna raises his wave with a mighty roar.
These Soma juices have flowed through the sheep’s woolly filters like celestial water-jars raining from the clouds;
like rivers rushing downward to the ocean, the pressed drops have been poured into the jars.
Flow onward, powerful as the host of Maruts, like the divine folk who are beyond reproach;
be swift with your favor toward us like waters, you who possess a thousand forms, like a sacrifice that conquers in battle.
Truly, thy laws are those of King Varuṇa; lofty and profound, O Soma, is thy domain.
Thou art pure, like the beloved Mitra; thou art to be honored like Aryaman, O Soma.
Like rain from heaven, this Soma, the purifying bearer, has flowed along his paths;
with a thousand streams, he has settled within us, upon the mother’s lap, and in the wooden vessel.
The King of rivers has clothed himself in his garment; he has mounted the straightest ship of Truth.
The drop has grown strong in the waters, urged by the hawk; the Father milks it, and he milks that which is born of the Father.
They approach the lion, the tireless one, the tawny and ruddy lord of this heaven, who is rich in sweetness.
The hero, foremost in battles, seeks out the cattle; the bull protects them all around with his eye.
They yoke to the chariot the formidable, tireless horse with honeyed back, vast-wheeled and lofty;
his sisters, the kinswomen, cleanse him, and those of common origin strengthen the vigorous steed.
Four milch-cows yielding ghee attend upon him, seated together within the same support;
they flow toward him while being purified with homage, and these many ones encompass him from every side.
The support of heaven and the foundation of earth, all the settlements are in his hand.
May there be for you, a source for the singer, a team of horses; the stalk of honey flows for Indra-power.
Winning the windless [strength] for the feast of the gods, O Soma, flow as the slayer of Vṛtra for Indra.
Bestow upon us great and most radiant wealth; may we be masters of heroic power.
Urged forward, the progenitor of heaven and earth has sped forth like a chariot seeking prize-winning strength;
going toward Indra, sharpening his weapons, he takes all treasures into his hands.
The voices of praise have cried out toward the three-backed bull, the bestower of vital strength;
clothing himself in the woods like Varuṇa among the rivers, the bestower of jewels distributes desirable treasures.
O you who lead a host of heroes, possessing all valiant men, victorious and powerful, flow on as a winner of riches;
armed with sharp weapons and a swift bow, unsubdued in battles, overcome the enemies in the fray.
Providing wide pastures and creating safety, flow toward the two united world-halves;
desiring to win the waters, the dawns, the sun, and the cattle, roar forth and gather for us great strengths.
O Soma, exhilarate Varuṇa; exhilarate Mitra; O Indu, Pavamāna, exhilarate Indra and Viṣṇu.
Exhilarate the host of Maruts; exhilarate the gods; O Indu, exhilarate the great Indra for his intoxication.

Thus, like a king, possessing wisdom, flow on with impetuous force, striking down all misfortunes; O Indu, bestow vital strength for our well-spoken hymn. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Like a neighing steed in a chariot-race, the first inspired thinker has been let loose by means of prayer;
the ten sisters drive the bearer upon the sheep-wool ridge toward his seats.
Pressed by the seers among the divine folk and by the descendants of Nahuṣa, Indu flows forth for the feast;
he who is immortal, being cleansed by mortal men with sheep’s wool, with milk, and with waters.
The bull, bellowing loudly for the bull, this Pavamāna stalk sends forth the bright milk of the cow;
the singer of thousands, knowing the words, the sun-like one traverses the fine mesh by stainless paths.
O Indu, as you are being purified, shatter the strongholds even of the Rākṣasas; spread out the spoils of victory.
With your swift weapon, strike down from above those who are near and those who are far—those who approach this sacrifice.
As in the ancient way, O possessor of all boons, prepare the forward paths for this new hymn.
May we, O doer of much, O provider of much food, overcome those great enemies who are difficult for the attacker to withstand.
Thus purifying yourself, grant us waters, light, and cattle, as well as many sons and grandsons;
O Soma, bestow upon us health, wide fields, and great lights, so that we may long behold the sun.
Being pressed, the golden stalk has been released into the filter like a chariot urged forward for the sake of gain;
being purified, it has attained Indra-like renown and has gratified the gods with offerings.
The seer, beholding men, has flowed toward the filter, assuming his name in his own womb;
settling in the vessels like a Hotṛ priest in his seat, the seven inspired Ṛṣis have approached him.
The wise Soma, the knower of the way, belonging to all the gods, goes forth constantly as he is purified.
He becomes the one who delights in all poetic inspirations; the sage exerts himself among the five peoples.
O Soma Pavamāna, all these thirty-three gods are within your secret place;
by their own powers, the ten [fingers] and the seven mighty rivers cleanse you upon the sheep's back.
May that indeed be the truth of Pavamāna, wherein all the singers gather together—
that light which he made for the day and the world, and which he protected Manu from the Dasyu, making him his adversary.

Like a Hotṛ priest going around the sacrificial enclosures rich in cattle, like a truthful king proceeding to assemblies, Soma, being purified, has gone to the jars; settling there like a wild buffalo in the forests.
The ten sisters, the flowing prayers of the sage, have cleansed him together as he is sprinkled.
The golden-hued one has run forth; born of the Sun, he has reached the vat like a prize-winning steed.
Like a crying infant with its mothers, the bull, much-desired, has flowed forth with the waters; like a youth going to a tryst with a maiden, he meets with the milk-cows in the jar.
And the udder of the cow has swelled; the wise Indu accompanies her with his streams. The cows mix the head [of the Soma] with milk in the vessels, as if with well-washed treasures.
O Indu, being purified, do thou, lowing with desire, bestow upon us wealth consisting of horses through the gods;
may Purandhi, eager and chariot-borne, come toward us to grant us riches.
Now, O Purifier, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroes, all-glittering and worthy of being protected by the wind.
O Indu, prolong the life of the singer; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
When the prayers vie for him, like beauties for a prize-winning steed, or as subjects for the sun;
choosing the waters, he flows on, acting as a seer, like one who opens a pen to increase the cattle—this is the sacred thought.
Twofold unfolding the abode of immortality, the worlds expand for him who finds the light of heaven.
Like cows swelling in the stall, the thoughts flowing toward the Law have lowed toward Indu.

When the sage bears his poetic insights around all the worlds like a hero on a chariot, he adorns glory among the gods for the sake of mortals; as a new source of wealth for skillful men, he abounds in many manifestations.
Born for glory, he has come forth from glory; he bestows glory and vital strength upon his singers.
Clothed in glory, they have attained immortality; their encounters become true when the measured course is run.
Flow toward us with nourishment and vigor; bring horses and cattle; create wide light and exhilarate the gods.
For all those things are easy for you to overcome; O Soma Pavamāna, you drive away our enemies.
The tawny one neighs loudly as he is released, settling within the belly of the wooden vessel while being purified;
guided by the men, he makes the cow his garment; therefore, generate hymns through your own inherent powers.
The golden-hued one, setting forth upon the path of Truth, sends forth his voice like a rower propelling a boat.
The god makes manifest the secret names of the gods upon the sacred grass for proclamation.
Like the surging waves of the waters, our inspired thoughts speed forth toward Soma;
bowing down, they approach him and, longing for him, enter into him who longs for them.
They milk that stalk, which is cleansed like a buffalo on a mountain ridge—the bull dwelling upon the mountains. To him, as he bellows, the prayers cling; Trita sustains Varuṇa within the ocean.
Impelling the voice like the Upavaktṛ priest of the Hotṛ, O Indu, as you are being purified, release our inspired thought.
When Indra and you both dwell together for our good fortune, may we be masters of heroic power.
The hero, leader of the chariots, goes at the head of the hosts seeking cattle; his army exults.
Making the invocations to Indra auspicious for his friends, Soma puts on his impetuous garments.
The bay steeds groom his bay horse with unceasing praises, sharpening him like racing horses.
As the friend of Indra, he mounts the chariot; the wise one approaches this gracious favor.
O God, flow for us through the service of the gods, O Soma, as food for the great Indra-drinking;
making the waters flow and raining down this heaven, purifying yourself, grant us wide space from the vast expanse.
Flow for invincibility, for non-slaughter, for well-being, and for great, complete attainment.
All these friends desire that; O Soma Pavamāna, I too desire that.
Soma flows clear, the progenitor of hymns, the progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth;
the progenitor of Agni, the progenitor of Sūrya, the progenitor of Indra, and the progenitor of Viṣṇu.
The Brahman of the gods, the path-maker of the poets, the seer of the sages, the buffalo of the wild beasts,
the hawk of the vultures, the axe of the forests— Soma goes forth singing across the filter.
Soma, while being purified, has caused the wave of speech, the songs, and inspired thoughts to surge forth like a river.
Beholding these lower enclosures from within, he stands among the cattle as a bull, knowing them well.

O Indu, as you flow for Indra, being exhilarating, victorious in battles, unassailed, and possessing thousandfold seed, pour forth toward the prize; O wise one, send up the wave of the stalk, impelling the cows.
The beloved Soma, favored by the gods, flows into the jar for Indra as a source of exhilarating joy.
With a thousand streams and a hundredfold strength, the drop goes forth like a prize-winning steed to the assembly.
Born as the ancient winner of wealth, being cleansed in the waters and milked from the stone,
the protector against curses and king of the world, he finds a path for the prayer as he is purified.

For by you, O Soma, our ancient fathers, the wise ones, performed their sacred rites, O Pavamāna. Winning [the prize] and unassailed, open wide the enclosures; be a bountiful patron to us with heroes and horses.
As you flowed for Manu, bestowing vital strength, slaying enemies, finding wide space, and accompanied by oblations—so flow now, conferring wealth; unite with Indra and bring forth our weapons.
Flow on, O Soma, rich in sweetness, observer of Truth, clothing yourself in waters upon the sheep’s-wool ridge.
Sit down within the wooden vats that are full of ghee—most exhilarating, intoxicating, the drink of Indra.
Flow with a hundred streams from heaven, winning a thousandfold, seeking booty at the feast of the gods;
bellowing together with the rivers in the jar, and with the milk-cows, prolonging our lifespan.
This very Soma, being purified by our prayers, like a prize-winning steed, overcomes hostilities;
he is like the fresh milk of Aditi, like a wide path, or like a well-guided draft-horse.
Well-armed and being purified by the pressers, flow toward your secret and lovely name;
like a courser seeking glory, flow toward booty, toward Vāyu, and toward the cows, O divine Soma!
The Maruts with their host cleanse and beautify the beloved infant as he is born, him who is the bearer of the sacrifice;
Soma, the seer, being himself a seer through his poetic songs and wisdom, goes singing across the filter.

He whose mind is that of a seer, who makes seers, the winner of light, whose leader is the thousandfold, the pathfinder of the poets—the mighty one, seeking to attain the third station, Soma shines as the sovereign king over the Virāj. *ṣṭup*.

The hawk dwelling in the bowls, the far-reaching bird, the drop that finds the cattle, bearing his weapons; following the wave of the waters toward the ocean, the buffalo proclaims his fourth station.
Like a handsome youth adorning his body, like a courser who has run for the winning of riches,
flowing around the vat like a bull toward the herds, he has entered the two bowls with a loud roar.
Flow on, O Indu, as Pavamāna with your greatness, bellowing as you flow through the woollen filters.
Entering the two bowls while being purified, sporting, may your exhilarating juice intoxicate Indra.

His great streams have been poured forth; anointed with the products of the cow, he has entered the jars. Creating the *sāman*, the wise singer of *sāmans* comes roaring toward his friend like one toward a sister.
Striking down the enemies, O Pavamāna, you go forth like a lover singing to his beloved;
Indu, like a bird swooping down upon the woods, Soma, being purified, settles within the jars.
O Soma, thy radiant beams, as thou art being purified, flow like a maiden—well-milking and with excellent streams.
The tawny one, brought hither, rich in boons, has bellowed within the waters in the jar of those who seek the gods.
Being purified by his impulse and his heat, the god has mingled his essence with the gods.
Pressed out, he goes around the filter chanting, like a Hotṛ-priest at measured stations rich in cattle.
Clothed in auspicious, well-fitting garments, the great seer, proclaiming the secret words,
flow into the two vessels while being purified— the far-seeing, ever-watchful one, at the banquet of the gods.
The beloved one is cleansed upon the sheep’s-wool back; he is the most glorious among the glorious, the ruler over us.
Flow toward us as you are being purified; do you gods protect us always with your blessings.
Sing forth and worship the gods; send forth the Soma for great wealth.
Sweet, he shall flow through the sheep's wool filter; seeking the gods, he shall sit within our jar.
The drop has approached the friendship of the gods; with a thousand streams it flows for exhilaration.
Praised by men according to the ancient ordinance, he has gone to Indra for great good fortune.
Flow, O tawny one, being purified, for the singer’s wealth; let your exhilarating juice go to Indra for his support.
Come on the same chariot with the gods toward our gift; do you all protect us always with blessings.
Proclaiming poetic wisdom like Uśanas, the god declares the generations of the gods;
he of mighty vows, whose kinship is pure, the purifier, approaches the stations, lowing like a wild boar.
Like swans, the bull-like hosts have gone toward the *tr̥pala* plant and toward wrath; they have come home.
O friends, together they sound forth the song of praise for the purifying one, the peerless hymn.
He hastens with the speed of the wide-striding one; like cows lowing, they measure him as he sports at will.
The sharp-horned one makes himself full of abundance; by day he appears golden, and by night he is ruddy.
The swift Indu flows, the Soma that brings a flood of cattle; he flows for Indra, inciting him to exhilaration.
He slays the Rakṣas, he drives away the enemies; creating wide space, the king of the host.
Then, mingled with honey in a stream, milked by the stones, Indu flows through the fleece;
the exhilarating god, enjoying the friendship of Indra, purifies himself for the intoxication of the god.
Being purified, the god flows toward his dear ones, bedewing the gods with his own juice;
Indu, clothing himself in his seasonal laws, has enveloped the ten fingers on the sheep’s back.
The red bull, bellowing toward the cows, goes forth making the earth and heaven resound;
like the roar of Indra, he is heard in the battle, and making this speech intelligible, he flows onward.
Worthy of being tasted, swelling with milk, you go forth impelling the honeyed stalk;
as Pavamāna, you go making a continuous sound, O Soma, being poured out for Indra.
Flow thus, O exhilarating one, for intoxication, bending down the weapons of the one who seizes with his hand;
bearing your radiant color all around, flow for us, O Soma, seeking cattle when poured out.
O Indu, having taken pleasure in us, flow on easy paths by fair ways, creating wide expanses;
striking away misfortunes on every side like a club, run over the high back upon the sheep’s wool.
Flow for us with divine rain that is swift-moving, nourishing, full of refreshment, and quickening;
like a loosened lock of hair, O Indu, flow along the desert, discerning these lower kin and vital breaths.
O Soma, as you are being purified, untie the knotted tangle like a knot; distinguish between the straight path and the crooked one.
Like a neighing bay horse, let loose, run hither like a young man, O God, dwelling in the waters.
O Indu, being welcomed for exhilaration by the gods, flow over the back of the sheepskin with your swelling stream.
With a thousand streams, fragrant and undeceived, flow around for the winning of booty in the contest of men.
Those which are without reins, without chariots, unyoked, like horses let loose in the race—these bright Soma drops flow; O gods, come near to them to drink.
Thus, O Indu, flow for us toward the feast of the gods, like a cloud of water into the vessels;
may Soma grant us desirable, vast, and formidable wealth, accompanied by heroic sons.
When the speech of the longing mind fashioned him, or when [he was born] under the law of the eldest upon the surface of the waters,
then the cows, lowing toward their choice, went to Indu in the jar as their beloved lord.
The celestial giver, swelling with gifts, flows for the sake of Truth; the wise one purifies himself for Truth.
He becomes the upholder of the law, the king of the assembly; he is borne across the earth by his ten rays.
Purifying himself with strainers, the one who beholds men, the king of both gods and mortals, has from of old become the lord of riches; the drop (Indu) bears the well-sustained and beautiful *ṛta*.
Like a courser toward glory and the winning of booty, flow toward the feast of Indra and Vāyu.
As such, grant us thousands of great refreshments; O Soma, being purified, become the finder of wealth for us.
May the Soma juices, which are to be poured out for the gods, flow toward our dwelling rich in heroes;
may they, seeking sacrifice, possessing all desirable things, and most delightful like the heavenly Hotṛ-priests, grant us their favor.
Thus, O God, flow for the sake of the gods, O Soma, for the great feast, as the drink of the gods;
for we indeed stand ready for the great battle. While being purified, make the two worlds well-established.
Like a neighing horse yoked with stallions, like a terrifying lion swifter than thought— by the straightest paths directed hitherward, flow for us, O Indu, as the source of well-being.
A hundred streams, born of the gods, have been released; sages cleanse these thousands of them.
O Indu, flow from heaven as a winner of gain; you are the leader of great wealth.

Like the outpourings of heaven, the streams of days have been released; the wise king does not violate his covenant with Mitra. Like a son following the will of his father, flow for this people, granting them security.
Your honeyed streams have been released, when, purified, you pass through the sheep's wool; O Pavamāna, you flow for the domain of the cows. Being born, you have made the sun swell with your hymns.
Roaring along the path of Truth, you, the bright one, shine forth as the abode of immortality.
As such, you flow for Indra, exhilarating and impelling the voice through the hymns of the sages.

O Soma, as a divine, well-winged bird, looking down and swelling with streams at the rite for the feast of the gods, O Indu, enter the vessel that holds the Soma; go bellowing toward the ray of the sun.
The bearer of the oblation sends forth three voices: the thought of Truth and the inspired wisdom of the sacred word.
Like cows seeking their master, they go toward the Lord of Cows; like lowing thoughts, the hymns go toward Soma.
The milch-cows low longingly toward Soma; the inspired poets, inquiring with their hymns, seek Soma.
Pressed and anointed, Soma is purified; to Soma the *arkas* and the *triṣṭubh* verses sing together in harmony.
Thus, O Soma, being poured out and purified, flow for our well-being;
enter into Indra with a mighty roar, strengthen our speech, and generate abundant wisdom.
The watchful sage, the Soma, being purified by the thoughts of the *ṛta*, has settled within the vessels;
him do the paired Adhvaryus, longing for him, serve—the charioteers with skillful hands.
Being purified, he has filled both worlds like the sun from its source; he has revealed them both.
He, whose dear ones are indeed beloved for his aid, shall surely grant wealth to the singer as if to a victor.
May he, the increaser who grows strong while being purified, the bounteous Soma, protect us with his light—
that by which our ancient fathers, knowers of the path and finders of heaven, heated the rock to win the cows.
The ocean has roared, established in the first ordinance, generating offspring as the king of the world.
As a bull upon the sheep’s-wool filter, the Soma, the pressed drop, has grown great on the high ridge.
Soma the mighty bull performed that great deed when, as the embryo of the waters, he chose the gods. As Pavamāna, he bestowed vigor upon Indra; as Indu, he generated light in the sun.
Exhilarate Vāyu for our desire and for bounty; exhilarate Mitra and Varuṇa as you are being purified.
Exhilarate the host of Maruts, exhilarate the gods, and exhilarate Heaven and Earth, O divine Soma!
Flow straight on, O crusher of the crooked, driving away disease and our adversaries;
blending your milk with the milk of the cows, you belong to Indra, and we are your friends.
Flow as the sweetener of honey, a fountain of wealth; flow to us with a hero and with fortune.
O Indu, being purified, be sweet for Indra; flow to us with riches from the ocean.

The pressed Soma flows in a stream like a swift horse let loose, like a river rushing down a slope; seeking the prize, he has settled in his wooden seat while being purified. The drop, Indu, has flowed together with the milk and together with the waters.
This very Soma, O Indra, flows for you into the vessels—wise, longing, and powerful;
he who is self-luminous, the charioteer, truly impetuous, and who has been released like the desire of those devoted to the gods.
Purifying himself with ancient vigor, assuming the forms of the daughter [of the sun],
and clothing himself in a triple-layered protection within the waters, he goes forth chanting like a Hotṛ priest at the assemblies.
Now, O divine Soma, flow as a chariot-steed for us, being purified into the two bowls—
sweetest in the waters, honeyed, true to the cosmic order, like the god Savitṛ whose thoughts are truth.
Flow toward Vāyu for his enjoyment, being praised; flow toward Mitra and Varuṇa while being purified;
flow toward the hero who speeds with prayer and stands upon the chariot; flow toward Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt.
Flow toward us with well-woven garments; being purified, flow toward us with cows that yield milk easily. O divine Soma, bring to us bright gold for our sustenance, and horses yoked to chariots.
Flow toward us with celestial treasures, and as you are being purified, flow toward all earthly riches;
flow toward that wealth by which we may obtain the heritage of the Ṛṣis, even as Jamadagni did for us.
Flow with this purification, purifying these riches; O Indu, flow forth into the lake so that it may be rich in food.
Even here, like the wind driven by the sun, let the one of many wisdoms grant a hero to the swift runner.
And so, flow for us with these purifications at the famous ford of Śravāyya;
may Naiguta shake down sixty thousand treasures for our delight, like ripe fruit from a tree.
Great indeed are his two names for the bull: *vṛṣan* and *śūṣa*.
Whether at the crushing or the piercing blow, he has sent the attackers to sleep and softened them; he has struck down the enemies and the senseless ones.
You go toward the three filters stretched out; you run along one as you are being purified.
You are Bhaga; you are the giver of the gift; you are Maghavan for the sake of the wealthy, O Indu.
This all-knowing, wise Soma flows as the king of the entire world;
sending forth his drops at the assemblies, Indu passes through the sheep's wool filter and goes on his way.
The undeceived buffaloes lick the drop; like eager poets at the station, they sing aloud.
The wise ones urge it forward with ten fingers and anoint its form with the essence of the waters.
O Soma, through you, the purifying one, may we continually gather the wealth that has been made for us in battle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
Flow toward us with wealth that best wins the prize, most desired by many— O Indu, wealth that brings a thousandfold gain, possessing great splendor and conquering all.
Being pressed, he has clothed himself in the sheep’s fleece as if in armor upon a chariot;
the drop, placed upon the wooden vessel, has flowed forth with his streams when urged on.
Being pressed, this Indu has flowed all around the sheep’s wool, distilling exhilaration;
rising up in streams at the sacrifice, he goes forth with brilliance, seeking the cattle.
For you indeed, O God, bestow wealth upon every mortal who offers oblations;
O Indu, you win for us thousandfold riches consisting of a hundredfold lives.
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Vasu, may we be the ones to receive from you this much-desired wealth;
O Adhrigu, may we be the very closest recipients of your nourishment and favor.
Twice do the five sisters, their own glory, bathe him who is struck by the mountain— the beloved, desirable, surging wave of Indra.
They purify with the fleece that beloved, golden-hued, brown one,
who goes to all the gods together with his exhilarating juice.
For by means of his protection, you drink [the soma] which accomplishes skill;
he who has established great renown among the patrons, like the beloved sun.
At your sacrifices, O two daughters of Manu, the drop was born for you both, O Heaven and Earth—
O goddesses dwelling on the mountains, that god has not failed you, O you of mighty sound.
O Soma, you are poured out for Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, to drink;
and for the hero who bestows sacrificial gifts, the god who sits upon his seat.
Those ancient Soma juices have flowed through the filter at the dawns; snorting away those who plot evil, they drive off the thoughtless ones at daybreak.
O friends, may you and we, the wise patrons, attain him who shines before us;
may we obtain him who possesses the fragrance of strength and win him whose home is strength.
For the beloved and bold one, they stretch out the bow as a manly deed; at the forefront of the inspired songs, the seekers of greatness weave a bright garment for the Asura.
Then, adorned by the night, he plunges toward the spoils of war,
when the prayers of Vivasvat urge the tawny steed to go forth.
We cleanse that exhilarating drink of his which is most beloved by Indra,
which the cows have yielded with their mouths in the past and which the wise ones yield now.
They have sung toward him as he is being purified with an ancient song;
and the prayers, bearing the names of the gods, have yearned for him.
They purify him, the sustaining one, as he flows through the sheep’s wool;
the wise ones direct him toward them, like a messenger, for the sake of their first thought.
Being purified, the most intoxicating Soma settles within the vessels;
like a bull depositing seed in a cow, he, the Lord, manifests his eloquence through our prayers.
Pressed for the gods, that god is cleansed by those of skillful deeds; he finds as he plunges into these great waters, which he has caused to flow together.
O Indu, pressed by the men and guided through the filter, you are led forth;
most intoxicating for Indra, you settle within the vessels.
The guileless mothers low toward the beloved, desirable [Soma] of Indra; like a calf born at the first age, they lick it with their tongues.
O Indu, being purified, bring hither, O Soma, wealth of double strength;
you nourish all treasures in the house of the donor.
Release the prayer yoked by the mind, as thunder releases the rain; O Soma, you cause the treasures of the earth and those of heaven to flourish.
Your stream flows around like that of a victor, as you are pressed; rushing through the woolly filter like a prize-winning steed seeking booty.
O Sage Soma, flow with your stream for our mental power and skill;
pressed for Indra to drink, and for Mitra and Varuṇa as well.
Flow, O Soma, most excellent winner of booty, with your stream into the filter, being pressed for Indra, for Viṣṇu, and for the gods— most rich in sweetness.
The guileless mothers lick you, the tawny one, in the filter; like milch-cows their newborn calf, O Pavamāna, they lick you in the supporting expanse.
O Pavamāna, you go toward great glory with your variegated rays;
boldly striking down all darkness in the house of the donor.
O you of mighty vows, you have surpassed both heaven and earth;
O Pavamāna, by your greatness, you have clothed yourself in your mantle.
Through the prior conquest of your soma-juice, for the exhilarating pressed drink—
O friends, drive away the dog, the long-tongued one.
He who, being pressed, flows all around with a purifying stream— the drop (indu) is like a horse that must be brought to its task.
The men, with all-encompassing thought, urge that Soma, difficult to master,
toward the sacrifice with the pressing-stones.
Pressed for Indra, the most honey-sweet and exhilarating Soma drops have flowed through the filter; may your intoxications go to the gods.
"Indu flows for Indra," thus the gods have declared;
the Lord of Speech exerts himself as a sacrifice, ruling over all by his might.
In a thousand streams the ocean flows, stirring the voice; Soma, the lord of riches, is the friend of Indra day by day.
This Pūṣan, this wealth, this Bhaga—Soma, being purified, flows on;
as the lord of the entire world, he has looked out upon both heaven and earth.
The dear, eager cows have lowed together for exhilaration;
the Soma drops, as they are purified, prepare the paths.
O Pavamāna, bring that which is most powerful and worthy of renown,
that which surpasses the five tribes, and by means of which we may win wealth.
The Soma drops flow clear for us, the best finders of the path;
pressed as friends, they are stainless, devout, and finders of the light.
Pressed out by the stones upon the ox-hide,
they who find wealth have resounded on all sides for us, bestowing nourishment.
These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curds, are beautiful to behold like suns; moving swiftly, they are firmly established in the clarified butter.
Let no mortal obstruct this speech of the pressed juice;
drive away the stingy dog, as the Bhr̥gus struck down Makha.
The kinsman has clothed himself in his garment like a son for enjoyment in the lap of his parents; he has sped forth like a lover to a maiden, like a suitor to take his seat upon the womb.
That hero, the accomplisher of skill, who has propped apart the two worlds—
he, the tawny one, the ordainer, has entered the filter to sit upon his seat like a priest.
Soma flows through the sheep’s woolly filter onto the ox-hide;
bellowing like a tawny bull, he goes toward Indra’s appointed place.
Acting as the child of the great ones, impelling the vision of the Eternal Order (Ṛta),
he has encompassed all dear things, even doubly so.
Near the two pressing-stones of Trita, he partook of that secret place;
then, through the seven stations of the sacrifice, he attained what is dear.
With the stream of Trita, he has sent forth wealth upon the three ridges;
the one of excellent wisdom measures out his paths.
When he was born, the seven mothers instructed the wise one for the sake of glory;
he, being firm, has taken notice of riches.
In his service, all the guileless gods are of one accord; their delights become desirable when they take pleasure in him.
That lovely germ which those who increase the cosmic order have brought forth for us to behold—
the sage, most bountiful, much-desired at the sacrifice.
The two great mothers of *ṛta*, moving together in harmony by their own nature,
when they anoint [the sacrifice], they extend the sacrifice in due order.
With wisdom and with bright eyes, you have opened the stall of heaven;
impelling the vision of Truth at the sacrifice.
To Soma, the purifying ordainer, let a song be raised;
with hymns, bring him sustenance as it were, so that he may take pleasure in them.
Anointed with the products of the cow, he flows through the sheep’s woolly filters;
being purified, the golden-hued one makes for himself his three dwelling places.
It flows around the honey-dripping vat through the sheep’s wool filter;
the seven voices of the seers have sung aloud to it.
The leader of hymns, the all-encompassing god who cannot be deceived,
Soma, the tawny one, being purified, flows into the two bowls.
Go along with the divine powers according to your own nature, on the same chariot as Indra;
being purified by the priests, O immortal one, together with the priests.
Like a courser seeking the prize, the god, pressed for the gods,
the all-pervading Pavamāna flows forth.
O friends, sit down and sing forth to the one being purified; adorn him with sacrifices for the sake of glory, as if adorning a child.
Bring together the one who wins the household, like a calf with its mothers,
toward the exhilarating drink that delights the gods and possesses double strength.
Purify that which accomplishes skillful action, so that it may be for the feast of the host,
and so that it may be most auspicious for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The voices have sung toward you, the finder of wealth, for our sake;
with cows we clothe your color.
O Indu, lord of our exhilarations, you are the celestial nymph of the gods;
like a friend to a friend, be the best finder of the path for us.
Drive away from us every demon and every devourer; keep the godless and the double-dealing man far from us, and remove our distress.
O friends, sing toward him as he purifies himself for your exhilaration; like a child, they sweeten him with sacrifices and hymns of praise.
Like a calf with its mothers, Indu, being urged forward, is anointed; the exhilarating drink, which delights the gods, is adorned by our prayers.
This is the means for skill; this is for the feast of the host;
this most honey-sweet juice has been pressed for the gods.
O Indu, flow forth when pressed, rich in cattle and horses, O thou of excellent skill;
I have placed thy bright color upon the cows.
O Indu, lord of our bay steeds, most delightful to the gods as their food,
be for our splendor like a friend to a friend, a hero.
O Indu, drive far away from us every godless devourer who seeks to harm; overcome the double-tongued oppressor and cast him out.
May these pressed, tawny drops go toward Indra, the bull;
born with speed, these Soma-drops find the light of heaven.
This pressed Soma, winning booty for the sake of Indra’s bearing, flows clear; it takes heed of victory, as one who knows how.
In the exhilarations of this [Soma], may Indra seize the winning grasp;
and may he, the winner of waters, wield the bull-like thunderbolt.
Flow forth, O Soma, you who are watchful; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Bring us brilliant vigor that finds the light of heaven.
Flow for Indra as a virile exhilarating draught, O you who are visible to all; you who possess a thousand paths, the maker of ways, the far-seeing one.
The best finder of the way for us, the most honey-sweet for the gods—
go forth with a thousand paths, bellowing aloud!
Flow on with your streams in your might for the feast of the gods, O Indu;
as the honeyed Soma, take your seat in our jar.
Your drops, floating upon the waters, have strengthened Indra for exhilaration;
the immortal gods have drunk you for the sake of immortality.
O pressed drops, being purified, flow wealth toward us— ye who cause rain from heaven, who set the waters flowing, and who find the light of heaven.
Soma, being purified, flows through the sheep’s wool with his wave;
as Pavamāna, he bellows at the forefront of the voice.
With their prayers they urge on the prize-winner who sports in the wood beyond the sheepskin;
the hymns have resounded together toward him of the triple back.
He has been let loose toward the jars like a prize-seeking steed in the contest; purifying himself and generating speech, he has flowed forth.
The beloved, golden-hued one flows with speed across the obstacles;
pouring forth glory accompanied by heroes for the sake of those who praise him.
Flow thus, seeking the gods; streams of sweetness have been poured forth.
Chanting, you pass through the filter from every side.
Pour out on every side the pressed juice, Soma, which is the supreme oblation;
he who, the friend of men, having flowed within the waters, has pressed the Soma with the stones.
Now, being purified by the sheep’s wool, flow around, unassailable and most fragrant.
Even when pressed in the waters, we exhilarate thee with the juice, blending thee, the superior one, with the milk of cows.
Being pressed for all to see, the exhilarating god-intoxicant, Indu, the far-seeing power of wisdom.
Being purified, O Soma, you flow with your stream, clothing yourself in the waters;
as a bestower of treasures, you sit upon the seat of Order—O God, a golden fountain.
Milking the heavenly udder for the dear honey, he has sat upon the ancient dwelling place;
the prize-winning one flows toward the desirable support, shaken by men, far-seeing.
Being purified, O Soma, the watchful one, dear to us, you pass through the sheep's wool filter;
you have become a sage, the best of the Aṅgirases—mingling our sacrifice with honeyed sweetness.
Soma, the bountiful, flows on as the best finder of the path, a seer, a sage, far-seeing.
You became a poet, most beloved by the gods; you caused the sun to ascend in heaven.
Soma, being pressed by the pressers upon the backs of the sheep’s wool, goes with a stream like a bay horse; he goes with a pleasant stream.
In the marshy land, Soma has flowed with cattle; he has flowed with cows that have been milked.
Like the ocean, they have gone to the enclosures; exhilarating, he pours out for intoxication.
O Soma, pressed by the stones, flow through the sheep’s woolly fleece;
like a man entering a city, the tawny one has entered the two bowls; you have taken your seat within the wooden vats.
He has cleansed himself through the fine wool of the sheep, like a prize-seeking steed at the contest;
Soma Pavamāna is to be celebrated by the wise, by the inspired singers and the chanters of hymns.
O Soma, for the banquet of the gods, you have swelled like a river with its flood;
with the milk of the stalk, exhilarating and wakeful, flow toward the honey-dripping vat.
The beloved one has clothed himself in a bright white garment; he is to be polished like a dear son. The skillful workers urge him forth with their hands, as one drives a chariot, into the rivers.
The Soma drops, the active ones, flow toward the intoxicating exhilaration;
upon the surface of the ocean, they—wise, exhilarating, and finders of heaven—flow forth.
Crossing the ocean with his wave, the purifying one, the king, the god, [fulfills] the lofty *ṛta*;
flowing according to the law (*dharman*) of Mitra and Varuṇa, he is urged forward toward the lofty *ṛta*.
Guided by men, the lovely, far-seeing king, the god of the ocean.
The exhilarating Soma, pressed for Indra who is accompanied by the Maruts, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool; him the Āyus cleanse.
Being purified in the vessels, generating inspired thought, the seer Soma rejoices among the gods;
clothing himself in the waters, superior with the products of the cow, he has clothed himself while settling within the wooden vats.
O Soma, O Indu, I have rejoiced in your friendship day by day.
Many things, O tawny one, come upon me; help me, pass beyond those enclosures.
And indeed, O tawny Soma, by night and by day I have sought thy friendship at the udder;
beyond the sun that burns with heat, we have flown away like birds.
Being cleansed by skillful hands, you send forth your voice in the ocean;
O Pavamāna, you flow toward us with abundant, golden-hued wealth that is desired by many.
Being cleansed in the sheep’s wool filter while purifying himself, the bull has bellowed in the wooden vat.
O Soma Pavamāna, being anointed with milk, you flow toward the appointed place of the gods.
Flow on for the winning of booty, toward all poetic insights;
O exhilarating Soma, you were the first to sustain the ocean for the sake of the gods.
O Soma, flow forth through the earthly realm and the celestial spheres according to your divine laws;
the inspired poets, O far-seeing one, urge you on with their prayers and hymns, you who are radiant and pure.
The purifying Soma-streams have been released through the filter in a continuous flow—
intoxicating, accompanied by the Maruts, the steeds of Indra— toward wisdom and sacrificial offerings.
Clothed in waters, Indu flows around the vat, urged on by the pressers;
generating light, he has made the exhilarating ones roar, as one who puts on a garment makes the cows low.
Flow clear, O Soma, most rich in sweetness, for Indra, as the best exhilarant that awakens the intellect;
flow as the great, most celestial exhilarant.
Having drunk of you, that bull acts like a bull;
having drunk of this finder of light, he, the well-omened one, has stepped forward toward the offerings, as Etaśa speeds toward the prize.
For you indeed, O Pavamāna, most resplendent one, have proclaimed the divine generations for the sake of immortality.
That by which Navagva Dadhyanc uncovered [the light], by which the sages attained their goal—
that [Soma] through which they have gained renown among the gods, in the favor of the beautiful nectar of immortality.
This very one, pressed out, flows with his stream through the sheep’s woolly filter as the most intoxicating;
he plays like a wave of waters.
He who by his might cleft the kine from within the rock that held the waters of the dawn—thou hast extended thy stall of cattle and horses; O bold one, break it open like a warrior clad in mail.
O presser, pour out the praise-song like a horse— [the song] that crosses the waters, that traverses the mid-air, that roars through the woods, and that floats upon the waters.
The bull with a thousand streams, increasing the milk, dear to the divine race—
he who, born of the *ṛta*, has grown strong by the *ṛta*, the king, the god, the lofty *ṛta*.
O Lord of food, shine forth with lofty splendor and glory, O God who loves the gods; open wide the central cask.
Flow forth, O most skillful one, pressed into the two bowls like a lord of the people who is the bearer of the clans.
Flow as the rain from heaven, flow as the stream of waters; quicken our prayers for the winning of cattle.
They have milked from heaven this very bull, distilling intoxication, with a thousand streams,
him who bears all treasures.
The immortal bull was born, engendering [all things] and scorching the darkness with light;
well-praised by the seers, he has assumed his triple-colored garment through his wondrous power.
He is pressed, he who is the bringer of treasures, who is the bringer of riches, who is the bringer of nourishments— Soma, who is the bringer of secure dwellings.
Of whomsoever Indra shall drink, of whomsoever the Maruts, or Bhaga with Aryaman;
by whomsoever we may bring Mitra and Varuṇa together—we bring Indra for great protection.
O Soma, most intoxicating and well-armed, directed by the men for Indra to drink,
flow on as the most honey-sweet.
Enter the heart of Indra, the receptacle of Soma, as rivers enter the ocean—
being well-pleasing to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the highest pillar of heaven.
Flow forth, O Soma, as something sweet for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, and for Bhaga.
O Soma, may Indra drink of you when pressed, for the sake of wisdom and skill, as well as all the gods.
Thus, as a bright celestial nectar, flow for the sake of great immortality and for the dwelling place.
Flow clear, O Soma, as a great ocean, the father of the gods, toward all abodes.
O bright Soma, flow pure for the gods, for heaven, for earth, and for the welfare of all creatures.
You are the sustainer of heaven, the bright nectar; flow as a prize-winning steed within the true ordinance.
Flow on, O Soma, radiant and with a fine stream, as the ancient one through the great sheep's wool.
Guided by men, born and purified, the exhilarating one who finds the light of heaven flows forth with all [his powers].
Indu, being purified and choosing progeny for us, shall grant us all riches.
Flow clear, O Soma, for wisdom and skill, like a groomed courser, a prize-winner, for the sake of wealth.
The pressers purify that juice of yours for exhilaration—the Soma—for great splendor.
They cleanse the infant, the tawny Soma, the drop for the gods, as he is born in the filter.
The lovely drop has flowed for exhilaration, the sage in the lap of the waters, for our good fortune.
He bears the beautiful name of Indra, by which he struck down all the Vṛtras.
All the gods drink of this [Soma], which has been mixed with milk and pressed by men.
Being pressed, he has flowed forth in a thousand streams across the filter, through the sheep’s woolly fleece.
He, the prize-winning steed with thousandfold seed, being cleansed by the waters and mixed with milk.
O Soma, go forth into the belly of Indra, pressed by the men and guided by the stones.
The prize-winning steed, Soma, has been released through the filter for Indra in a thousand streams.
They anoint this Indu with the essence of honey for Indra, the bull, for his exhilaration.
For the gods, they cleanse thee, the tawny one, who art clothed in the waters, for thy spontaneous splendor.
The drop flows for Indra; it flows down, the fierce one, mixing itself as it releases the waters.
Flow forth indeed for the winning of booty, you who overcome all obstacles;
crossing over our enemies, you hasten toward us like one seeking to recover a debt.
For we rejoice after thee, O Soma, when thou art pressed, for the sake of great sovereignty over the battle;
O Pavamāna, thou plungest forward toward the spoils of war.
For you, O Pavamāna, have generated the sun and the milk in the expanse by your power,
hastening with the cow-inspiring and city-opening wisdom.
He has generated the immortal among mortals, according to the law of the nectar of the beautiful *Ṛta*; ever-flowing, he hastens toward the prize to win it.
For you have pierced through with glory every single inexhaustible spring that men drink from,
like one who carries arrows in his two hands.
Then some, beholding his kinship, the celestial ones, radiant with wealth, have sung aloud to him;
as Savitṛ, the god, uncovers the treasure.
O Soma, in thee the first ones who have spread the sacrificial grass have fixed their thought for great strength and for glory;
as such, O hero, impel us toward heroic power.
The ancient nectar of heaven, which is worthy of praise, they have milked forth from the great depth of the sky;
they raised a shout together toward Indra as he was being born.
And when, O Pavamāna, you pervade these two worlds, heaven and earth, and all these beings with your might,
you spread abroad like a bull standing over his herd.
Soma, being purified in the sheep’s wool filter, flows like a child at play;
the purifying drop, with its thousand streams and hundredfold strength, has flowed forth.
This Soma-drop, being purified in the stream of Truth, flows as a sweet wave for Indra;
it is the winner of booty, the finder of wide space, and the bestower of vital strength.
Flow on, O Soma, overcoming those who attack us, driving away the demons and difficult obstacles; well-armed and victorious, subdue our enemies.
With this golden luster, purifying himself, he overcomes all hostilities with his self-yoked steeds, like the sun with his self-yoked steeds.
The stream of the pressed juice shines as he purifies himself, the ruddy, tawny one;
when he encompasses all forms with the chanters, with the seven-mouthed chanters.
You find that treasure of the Paṇis; you cleanse yourself with your mothers in your own home, by means of the insights of the Eternal Order (Ṛta) within the home.
Like a chant from afar, that melody is where the insights rejoice.
Shining brightly, he bestows vital strength through the threefold ruddy [rays]; shining brightly, he bestows vital strength.
He moves, observing keenly, along the eastern quarter; the beautiful chariot strives with its rays, the divine chariot, the beautiful chariot.
Hymns have come forth, exalting Indra for victory, so that you two may become unshakable—the thunderbolt and you—unshakable in battles.
Various indeed are our thoughts, and diverse are the religious observances of men;
the carpenter seeks what is broken, the physician seeks the sick, and the priest seeks one who presses the Soma. Flow, O Indu, for Indra!
With aging plants and with the feathers of birds, the smith, working day after day with stones, seeks to fashion a golden vessel; for Indra, O Indu, flow around!
I am a singer, a physician, and a woman who grinds stones with her feet;
with various thoughts and seeking wealth, we follow thee like cattle—O Indu, flow around for Indra.
The horse is the drawer of the easy chariot; the frogs are the whisperers of laughter.
The penis desires the two hairy testicles, as a man desires water. Flow, O Indu, for Indra!
Let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma at Śaryaṇāvat;
bestowing strength within himself, he shall perform great heroic deeds. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Flow hither, O Soma, lord of the quarters, bountiful one from Ārjīka!
Pressed with the word of truth, with reality, with faith, and with austerity—O Indu, flow around for Indra.
The daughter of the Sun brought that bull, who had grown strong through Parjanya;
the Gandharvas received him, and they placed that essence in the Soma—O Indu, flow around for Indra!
Speaking the *ṛta*, O you whose splendor is *ṛta*; speaking the truth, O you whose deeds are true;
speaking with faith, O King Soma, you who are adorned by the Creator—O Indu, flow forth for Indra!
The flowing streams of the truly mighty and vast one flow together;
the juices of the flavorful one come together as he is purified by prayer, O golden-hued one. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Wherein the Brahman, O Pavamāna, speaking the metrical word, is exalted by the pressing-stone at the Soma; generating bliss through the Soma, flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where there is eternal light, in that world where the sun is established—place me there, O Pavamāna, in the immortal, undecaying world; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
Where King Vaivasvata dwells, where the enclosure of heaven is, where those mighty waters are—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
Where there is movement at will in the triple vault, the third heaven of the sky, where the worlds are full of light—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow for Indra.
Where desires and longings are fulfilled, where is the summit of the sun, where self-sustenance and satisfaction abide—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow for Indra.
Where joys and delights, pleasures and ecstasies abide, where the desires of desire are attained—there make me immortal; O Indu, flow around for Indra.
He who has stepped along the stations of the purifying *indu*—him they call "one of noble progeny," O Soma, he who has honored your mind. Flow around for Indra, O *indu*.
O Sage Kaśyapa, increasing the songs with the hymns of the mantra-composers, pay homage to King Soma, who was born as the Lord of plants; O Indu, flow forth for Indra.
The seven directions have various suns; there are seven hotṛ priests as officiants;
there are the seven Āditya gods—with them, O Soma, protect us. Flow around for Indra, O Indu!
O King, with that oblation of yours which has been prepared, protect us, O Soma!
Let not the malevolent overcome us, nor let anything whatsoever afflict us; flow around for Indra, O Indu!
